signals.topic: Subagent定义覆盖被SDK忽略，导致内置定义始终生效，Haiku子代理在大型MCP工具场景下完全失效
signals.summary: 用户通过options.agents自定义subagent定义(如Explore)，但SDK在初始化时pre-populate内置定义，Array.find()返回第一个匹配(内置定义)，覆盖被忽略。影响：Haiku默认Explore代理在工具定义接近200K tokens时完全崩溃，多个工作区均受影响。
aliases: Explore agent broken with large MCP tools
built-in agent definition always used over custom
signals.review_reason: 核心工作流阻断：用户无法通过SDK自定义subagent行为，导致Haiku子代理在生产环境中完全失效（工具定义>200K tokens时）。PostHog团队有多个生产项目受影响，提供了详细的root cause分析和临时patchwork证明问题可定位修复。

source_issues.title: Bug: subagent definition overrides are ignored; large MCP tools break Haiku in Claude Code
source_issues.evidence: PostHog团队生产环境受影响，提供了root cause分析(Array.find()总是返回内置定义)和4种workaround(含SDK patch)；截图显示Claude Code中Haiku Explore代理在大型MCP工具下完全崩溃；作者明确指出'无任何方式覆盖子代理行为'

signals.topic: Claude Code CLI在Node.js环境下运行时因未保护的Bun全局引用导致间歇性崩溃，错误无stderr输出极难诊断
signals.summary: SDK默认在Node.js上启动CLI，但CLI bundle包含未保护的Bun.which()等直接引用，导致间歇性ReferenceError。崩溃时仅返回exit code 1，无stderr输出，必须通过--debug-file才能捕获实际错误，极大延长MTTR。
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断性崩溃：SDK默认在Node.js上运行CLI，但CLI bundle中未保护的Bun引用导致间歇性进程退出。错误无stderr输出使得该问题极难诊断（用户必须配置debug-file才能定位），严重影响生产环境稳定性。

source_issues.title: Claude Code CLI crashes with ReferenceError: Bun is not defined when spawned under Node.js
source_issues.evidence: SDK默认在Node.js spawn CLI，cli.js bundle中包含未typeof保护的Bun引用；崩溃无stderr输出(exit code 1)，需额外配置--debug-file才能诊断；提供了root cause位置(function vCq)；workaround要求用户安装Bun并强制设置executable: 'bun'

signals.topic: 文件定义的subagent(.claude/agents/)在SDK的query()中无法作为可调用subagent类型被发现，0.2.87起回归
signals.summary: 自0.2.87起，通过.claude/agents/定义的文件型subagent可以被主代理'看到'(出现在上下文)，但Agent工具调用时报错类型不可用，回退到general-purpose ad-hoc代理，完全绕过文件型代理配置的model/tools/skills设置。
signals.review_reason: 关键功能回归：文件型subagent是SDK官方文档推荐的配置方式，但0.2.87起完全失效。主代理能看到agent定义但无法调用，被迫回退到无配置的general-purpose代理，实际使用了错误的model和toolset，行为与用户预期严重不符。

source_issues.title: File-based agents from .claude/agents/ not discovered as invocable subagent types (regression since ~0.2.87)
source_issues.evidence: 明确标记为0.2.87引入的regression(0.2.85正常)；文件型代理内容被加载到主代理上下文但未注册为可调用类型；主代理回退到general-purpose代理而非调用配置的haiku+自定义工具

signals.topic: MCP服务器进程在session结束后不清理，累积形成僵尸进程导致内存泄漏和端口冲突
signals.summary: query()内部spawn的MCP服务器进程在session结束(正常/超时/错误)后均未清理。外部编排器无法获取MCP进程PID，无法关联session与进程。并发场景下PID diff方案失效，导致node.exe/python.exe进程持续累积，内存持续增长，最终可能端口冲突。
signals.review_reason: 资源泄漏导致系统稳定性下降：MCP进程在session结束后不清理，随使用时间累积导致内存持续增长(数百MB级别)并可能端口冲突，在并发/relay编排场景下问题最为严重。

source_issues.title: query(): MCP server processes remain as zombies after session ends
source_issues.evidence: relay编排模式下5-10轮后数十个MCP进程(node.exe, python.exe)累积；用户使用wmic workaround但仅适用于单任务，并发场景下无法区分进程归属；SDK未暴露MCP进程PID也未保证清理

signals.topic: retryWithBackoff retries deterministic non-retryable errors (401, 4xx), wasting ~35 seconds per failure
signals.summary: Two separate code locations (github-file-ops-server.ts around lines 373/588 and token exchange) use retryWithBackoff but throw non-retryable errors (401 Unauthorized, 400 Bad Request, 404, 422) from inside the operation lambda. The throw does not prevent retry — all errors are caught unconditionally and retried up to 3 times with 5-20s backoff, wasting ~35 seconds on errors that will never succeed.
aliases: non-retryable errors not short-circuited in retry loop
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports confirm the same retry design flaw across two code paths (file ops server and token exchange). Deterministic failures (wrong token config, bad requests) are retried 3 times, adding ~35s of wall-clock waste per failure. This is a clear algorithmic bug, not a rare edge case.

source_issues.title: retryWithBackoff: non-retryable intent in github-file-ops-server.ts is unenforced
source_issues.evidence: Throwing from inside the retryWithBackoff operation lambda does NOT prevent retry. Errors are caught unconditionally. 400/404/422 on git ref updates are retried despite being deterministic failures, wasting ~35 seconds per failure.

source_issues.title: Don't retry non-retryable errors (401, 4xx) in retryWithBackoff
source_issues.evidence: App token exchange with 401 on 'Workflow validation failed' is retried 3 times with 5s+10s+20s backoff = ~35 seconds wasted on a deterministic failure.

signals.topic: MCP servers listed in allowedTools are never connected at runtime, making MCP tools permanently unavailable
signals.summary: When MCP servers (e.g. Notion) are specified via --mcp-config and listed in allowedTools, the action never actually connects to those servers at runtime. Claude returns NOTION_MCP_UNAVAILABLE and ToolSearch cannot find mcp__notion__* tools, making MCP integration completely non-functional despite correct configuration.
aliases: MCP server not connecting despite allowedTools config
signals.review_reason: MCP integration is a key feature of claude-code-action. When configured correctly (--mcp-config + allowedTools), the tools are silently unavailable at runtime — this is a complete functional failure of the MCP feature, not a minor edge case. User has verified NOTION_MCP_UNAVAILABLE in logs with correct env vars set.

source_issues.title: External MCP servers (e.g. Notion) listed in allowedTools but never connected at runtime
source_issues.evidence: Notion MCP tools present in SDK options.allowedTools but Notion MCP server is never connected at runtime. Claude returns NOTION_MCP_UNAVAILABLE. MCP integration completely non-functional.

signals.topic: No npm registry configuration for air-gapped/enterprise environments causes bun install to hang indefinitely
signals.summary: In enterprise/air-gapped environments, bun install hangs indefinitely because it cannot reach registry.npmjs.org. There is no action input to redirect bun install to an internal npm mirror (Artifactory, Nexus), causing GitHub Actions jobs to timeout with zero progress.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow failure for enterprise users. The action's dependency installation hangs and the job eventually times out, blocking the entire workflow. This is a common real-world requirement for corporate environments.

source_issues.title: feat: add input to configure npm registry for air-gapped / enterprise environments
source_issues.evidence: bun install hangs indefinitely in air-gapped environments because it cannot reach registry.npmjs.org. Job timeout occurs with no progress. Users must manually write ~/.npmrc in a pre-step as the only workaround.

signals.topic: cpSync crashes with ENOENT when sensitive paths (CLAUDE.md) are symlinks, causing action to abort
signals.summary: Since v1.0.89, when any SENSITIVE_PATHS (e.g. CLAUDE.md) is a symlink, restoreConfigFromBase crashes with 'ENOENT: no such file or directory, symlink' because cpSync defaults to dereference:false and tries to recreate the symlink before the parent directory exists.
aliases: symlink handling breaks action in v1.0.89
signals.review_reason: Action crashes (not just fails gracefully) due to a regression in v1.0.89 when CLAUDE.md is a symlink — a common organizational pattern. This is a main-flow blocking bug for any repo using symlinks, with a clearly identified root cause and regression commit.

source_issues.title: cpSync crashes with ENOENT when sensitive paths are symlinks
source_issues.evidence: Action crashes during restoreConfigFromBase with ENOENT when CLAUDE.md is a symlink. Introduced in PR #1174. Specific error: 'ENOENT: no such file or directory, symlink'. Action aborts completely.

signals.topic: GitHub App token expires after ~1 hour, causing 401 on all subsequent operations and total loss of job progress
signals.summary: After approximately 1 hour of job runtime, the GitHub App token expires. Subsequent operations (commits, comments, branch creation) all return 401 Unauthorized. The branch was never created, so all progress during the long-running job is completely lost with no artifact saved.
aliases: GitHub token expires after 1 hour loses all progress
token expiry causes data loss in long jobs
signals.review_reason: This is a critical data-loss bug. After ~1 hour of work, the entire job's output is discarded because the token expired and all git operations fail. For long-running jobs (which are precisely the ones that need Claude Code most), this represents total loss of user work.

source_issues.title: 401 GitHub after 1 hour job, no branch no commits, no comment update
source_issues.evidence: Job ran for over 1 hour then failed with 401 on GitHub operations. No branch was created, no commits were made, no comments posted. All progress in the long job was lost. User explicitly states 'all progress was lost'.

signals.topic: API validation fails with hard-coded Haiku model for users without Haiku access
signals.summary: The security-review action uses a hard-coded model string (claude-3-5-haiku-20241022) in the validate_api_access() call. When the configured claude-model is valid and available to the user but the hard-coded Haiku model is not, the action fails with a 404 not_found_error before the actual review even begins. This completely blocks the main workflow for affected users.
aliases: hard-coded Haiku model causes 404 validation failures
API access validation blocks workflow for non-Haiku users
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user workflow blocker. The hard-coded Haiku model in validate_api_access() causes a 404 error that prevents the entire security-review action from running — even when the user has correctly configured a valid model. The issue provides complete reproduction steps showing the workflow fails at validation before any review work begins. This meets the pain point definition: main flow is blocked and key functionality (security review action) is unavailable. While count=1 prevents a P0 rating per the hard constraint, the severity is high: every CI run fails for users without Haiku access, and the error is confusing because the configured model is valid.

source_issues.title: Make API validation model configurable instead of hard-coding claude-3-5-haiku-20241022
source_issues.evidence: User workflow explicitly sets claude-model: claude-sonnet-4-20250514, which is valid, but validation fails with '404 not_found_error: model: claude-3-5-haiku-20241022'. Full reproduction steps and error logs provided. Action fails before review starts.

signals.topic: asyncRewake hook output displays as raw <system-reminder> block in terminal instead of silent context injection
signals.summary: When a SessionStart hook with type asyncRewake returns output, it renders as a visible <system-reminder> XML/JSON block in the terminal prompt, leaking structured internal data to users. The hook's intended silent context injection path fails and falls through to an error rendering path.
aliases: SessionStart asyncRewake output visible in terminal
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed user-facing bug in Claude Code's hook system. Hook output that should be silently injected as context is instead rendered as visible raw XML/JSON in the terminal, exposing internal data structures. With count=2 (two independent reporters, one marked as duplicate of the other), it clearly affects multiple users. The bug defeats the purpose of the asyncRewake hook mechanism entirely.

source_issues.title: asyncRewake hook output renders as visible <system-reminder> in terminal
source_issues.evidence: Hook with asyncRewake type returns valid output, but the terminal shows raw <system-reminder> block with hookSpecificOutput JSON instead of injecting context silently. The Stop hook blocking error message suggests the asyncRewake type falls through to an error handling path.

source_issues.title: asyncRewake hook output displayed as visible system-reminder in terminal prompt
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed reproduction: SessionStart hook with asyncRewake: true returns hookSpecificOutput as visible <system-reminder> block in terminal prompt. The hook itself works (model receives context), but raw JSON is exposed to user.

signals.topic: Prompt cache not functioning causes excessive token consumption on simple requests
signals.summary: The prompt cache mechanism is not being utilized, causing every message — even trivial ones like 'hello' in an empty folder — to be processed from scratch, consuming 16,000-26,000 tokens per request. This results in severe cost inflation and quality degradation compared to expected cache-hit behavior.
signals.review_reason: Two independent reporters show the prompt cache is failing to activate, causing token costs of 16K-26K per trivial request instead of cache-hit pricing. This is a direct monetary cost impact (quota/cost category) that users can observe and measure. The cache is a core cost-saving mechanism — its failure means users are paying full price for every interaction.

source_issues.title: Excessive token consumption and quality degradation in recent builds
source_issues.evidence: User reports tokens burning excessively and quality dropping over recent weeks. Error logs include 429 rate limit errors and cache-related issues. User is on v2.1.92 and the pattern has been worsening.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Prompt cache not being utilized, causing excessive token consumption on simple requests
source_issues.evidence: User reports prompt cache completely broken. Every message consumes 16,000-26,000 tokens on a simple 'hello' in an empty folder with no special configuration. Clear direct evidence of cache miss on every request causing severe cost inflation.

signals.topic: Upgrade/update command fails with 429 error, blocking users from updating Claude Code
signals.summary: The 'claude upgrade' command fails with HTTP 429 (rate limit) when fetching from the Google Cloud Storage distribution URL, preventing users from updating to the latest version. The error is unrecoverable — retrying doesn't help.
signals.review_reason: The update mechanism is a critical main-flow path for a CLI tool. A 429 rate-limit error on the distribution endpoint makes the built-in upgrade path completely unusable for affected users. While count=1, the issue is a hard regression in the upgrade path — this is equivalent to a startup/major-flow failure for the product's self-update mechanism.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Upgrade to 2.1.94 is broken
source_issues.evidence: User on v2.1.92 runs 'claude upgrade' and gets: 'Error: Failed to install native update / Error: Failed to fetch version from https://storage.googleapis.com/claude-code-dist-.../claude-code-releases/latest: Request failed with status code 429'. This is a regression — upgrade worked in a previous version. Blocks the primary update mechanism.

signals.topic: Plugin auto-update with HTTPS git credentials missing hangs and freezes the entire Claude Code session
signals.summary: When a plugin with autoUpdate: true references a private GitHub repo via HTTPS and no HTTPS credentials are available, git blocks indefinitely waiting for interactive input on a non-existent TTY. This freezes the entire Claude Code session after the first response with no error message, no recovery path, and no way to unfreeze.
aliases: session freeze git clone credential prompt
signals.review_reason: This is a session-blocking bug: the entire Claude Code session becomes permanently frozen with no error message and no recovery path once triggered. The root cause (missing GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 on git subprocesses for plugin auto-update) is specific and reproducible. Users must manually clean up temp directories and reconfigure git auth to recover. This is a critical degradation of the core workflow.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Plugin auto-update hangs entire session when HTTPS git credentials are missing
source_issues.evidence: User with a plugin pointing to a private HTTPS GitHub repo and no HTTPS credentials (SSH-only auth via gh) experiences complete session freeze. The session can send one message and get one response, then is permanently frozen. No error shown to user. A temp_git_* directory is left with zero commits. Git process visible in ps aux, stuck waiting for credentials. Workaround requires 'gh auth setup-git' and manual temp directory cleanup.

signals.topic: Mid-session model update causes performance regression: degraded output quality and higher token usage
signals.summary: During long sessions (12+ hours), a mid-session model update causes a sharp performance drop — features that previously required single-pass implementation now need 3-5 rounds of corrections, the model misses obvious issues, leaves debug code in production, and token consumption increases. The quality gap is stark and immediately noticeable to users.
aliases: performance degradation after update long session
signals.review_reason: This is a clear workflow regression for long-running sessions. The user provides detailed before/after behavioral evidence showing the same model version (Opus 4.6) producing substantially worse output quality and higher token usage after a mid-session update. While count=1, the evidence is specific and the impact is severe — it undermines trust in long Claude Code sessions for serious development work.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Performance Degradation After Mid-Session Update
source_issues.evidence: User ran a 12+ hour session, established strong baseline performance (single-pass implementations of RSVP system, security audit, deploy pipeline, etc.), then experienced a mid-session model update. Post-update: features required 5+ retry rounds instead of 1 pass, model missed obvious issues, left console.log in production, and consumed significantly more tokens. Contrast with pre-update performance was stark and immediately noticeable.

signals.topic: LLM-based grading example uses substring check causing all answers to be graded as correct
signals.summary: The `grade_completion` function in the LLM-based grading documentation example uses `"correct" in grader_response.lower()` which matches "correct" as a substring of "incorrect", causing 100% false-positive accuracy regardless of answer correctness.
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user pain point: the official LLM-based grading documentation example produces systematically wrong evaluation results. Users copy-pasting this code will see 100% accuracy regardless of answer correctness, completely defeating the purpose of evaluation. The bug is reproducible and well-documented with a full code example, a clear root cause (substring matching), and a concrete fix. While count=1 and single-repository, the review_reason provides strong user impact evidence: the evaluation system is fundamentally broken and will mislead any user relying on it.

source_issues.title: [BUG] False positive in LLM-based grading example
source_issues.evidence: Bug report provides full reproduction steps demonstrating that with an intentionally wrong golden_answer ('The capital of Japan is Madrid'), the grader still returns 'correct' because 'correct' is a substring of 'incorrect'. The issue explicitly shows the function returns 'correct' for every response, resulting in 100% score even with wrong answers.

signals.topic: Custom MCP connector stuck on 'syncing' indefinitely in Claude Desktop organization admin
signals.summary: Custom MCP connectors added via Claude for Organizations admin panel get stuck on 'syncing' forever and never connect, even when the server is healthy and all tools register correctly. The connector cannot be used at all — a complete block of the custom connector feature.
signals.review_reason: Custom MCP connector feature is completely blocked — stuck on 'syncing' and never resolves regardless of redeploys or restarts. User cannot use the connector at all after adding it via the org admin panel. This is a clear main-flow failure with no workaround.

source_issues.title: Custom connector stuck on 'syncing' in Claude Desktop — organization plugin
source_issues.evidence: Connector shows 'syncing' spinner indefinitely; quitting/reopening, toggling, and multiple server redeploys (v37-v40) do not resolve it. Server is confirmed healthy. Feature completely unusable.

signals.topic: hookify tool_matcher fails to match any MCP tool due to unstripped server UUID prefix
signals.summary: Hookify rules written with short tool names never match MCP tools because Claude Code dispatches MCP tools with a 'mcp__<uuid>__<name>' prefix, while rule matching does exact string comparison. All hookify safety rules silently fail for every MCP tool, leaving critical operations (Slack sends, calendar mutations) completely unblocked.
aliases: MCP tool names not matched by hookify
signals.review_reason: Hookify safety rules silently fail for all MCP tools — this is a critical security/control gap where configured rules have zero enforcement. The failure is silent (rules load, hooks fire, but matching never succeeds), making it particularly dangerous for users relying on hookify to gate side-effecting MCP operations.

source_issues.title: [hookify] tool_matcher does not match MCP tools (server UUID prefix not normalized)
source_issues.evidence: Silent failure: rules load and hooks dispatch, but matching never succeeds. All MCP tools bypass hookify rules regardless of configuration. Safety-critical rules for side-effecting tools (Slack, calendar) have zero enforcement.

signals.topic: iMessage plugin race condition permanently drops RCS/SMS messages during poll
signals.summary: The iMessage plugin's poll query uses an INNER JOIN on chat_message_join, causing a race condition where messages are permanently lost if the join row is written after the message row. Evidence shows 2,188 orphaned messages in production. RCS messages are disproportionately affected, with real-time notifications missed while history queries still work.
signals.review_reason: Messages are permanently lost in production — not delayed or retriable, but gone forever due to a race condition in the poll query. The INNER JOIN pattern means once the watermark advances past an unjoined ROWID, that message is never checked again. This is a critical data-loss bug affecting real-time notifications.

source_issues.title: iMessage plugin: race condition in poll query causes missed RCS/SMS messages
source_issues.evidence: Production evidence: 2,188 orphaned messages with no corresponding chat_message_join entry. RCS contacts experience intermittent notification failures despite history queries working fine. Messages are permanently lost, not just delayed.

signals.topic: Vercel plugin sends bash commands via telemetry even when user has explicitly disabled opt-out
signals.summary: The Vercel plugin ignores the user's 'disabled' telemetry preference for base events. When a user sets telemetry-preference to 'disabled', only trackEvent (prompt text) is blocked; trackBaseEvents (bash commands, session metadata, device IDs) is always sent. Bash commands may contain server IPs, database hosts, branch names, PR titles — violating user privacy expectations.
signals.review_reason: User privacy violation: users who explicitly opt out of telemetry have their bash commands (containing potentially sensitive server IPs, database hosts, branch names) sent to Vercel anyway. The trackBaseEvents function has no preference check at all, making the opt-out mechanism entirely ineffective for the most data-sensitive category (bash commands).

source_issues.title: [vercel] trackBaseEvents bypasses user's telemetry "disabled" preference — bash commands sent without opt-out
source_issues.evidence: Code analysis shows trackBaseEvents has zero preference checks. Bash commands (potentially containing server IPs, DB hosts, branch names, PR titles) and device IDs are sent unconditionally despite user opt-out. Workaround of adding 127.0.0.1 for telemetry.vercel.com is the only escape hatch.

signals.topic: Discord plugin intermittent 'channel not allowlisted' errors despite correct configuration
signals.summary: The Discord plugin's reply tool fails intermittently with 'channel is not allowlisted' errors even when access.json is correctly configured. The root cause is that fetchTextChannel() hits the Discord API directly without a cache-first strategy or retry logic, so transient WebSocket disruptions cause the API call to fail and propagate a misleading error. Core functionality is unreliable.
signals.review_reason: Discord plugin reply functionality fails intermittently with misleading error messages, making the core reply feature unreliable during real usage. The error ('channel not allowlisted') incorrectly implies a configuration problem when the real cause is transient WebSocket issues. Users have no way to distinguish real config errors from transient failures.

source_issues.title: Discord plugin: intermittent "channel not allowlisted" errors due to unstable channels.fetch()
source_issues.evidence: Replies succeed for a while then fail repeatedly for minutes before recovering, with no config change. The misleading error message ('not allowlisted') masks the real root cause (WebSocket disruption). No cache-first lookup or retry logic exists in fetchTextChannel().

signals.topic: claude-api skill description truncated (>250 chars) causes incorrect skill triggering for non-Anthropic SDKs
signals.summary: The claude-api skill description exceeds 250 characters, causing Claude Code to truncate it and hide the DO NOT TRIGGER conditions. This leads to incorrect skill invocation when users work with OpenAI or other non-Anthropic AI SDKs.
aliases: skill description too long causes wrong triggers
signals.review_reason: The truncated description means the claude-api skill's exclusion conditions are hidden, causing it to incorrectly trigger for OpenAI and other non-Anthropic AI SDK code. This is an active functional defect affecting any user working with multiple AI SDKs in Claude Code.

source_issues.title: claude-api skill description truncated in Claude Code listings
source_issues.evidence: The claude-api skill description exceeds 250 characters, causing Claude Code to truncate it. The DO NOT TRIGGER when conditions are cut off, meaning Claude may incorrectly invoke the skill when working with non-Anthropic AI SDKs (OpenAI, etc.). This is an active functional misbehavior, not a theoretical concern.

signals.topic: Git LFS mismatch for shadcn-components.tar.gz causes git pull --rebase to fail in parent repos using this as a submodule
signals.summary: The shadcn-components.tar.gz file is committed as a raw binary blob despite .gitattributes tracking *.tar.gz with LFS. This creates a dirty working tree on every checkout, and when the repo is used as a submodule, git pull --rebase fails with 'fatal: cannot rebase with locally recorded submodule modifications'.
aliases: LFS pointer mismatch submodule rebase failure
signals.review_reason: This bug breaks a fundamental git workflow for any user or organization that incorporates this repo as a submodule. The git pull --rebase failure is a complete blocker for keeping the submodule up to date, forcing an unacceptable workaround.

source_issues.title: Git LFS mismatch for shadcn-components.tar.gz breaks submodule usage
source_issues.evidence: File committed as raw binary blob but .gitattributes tracks *.tar.gz with LFS filter. Every checkout produces a dirty working tree. When used as a submodule, git pull --rebase in the parent repo fails with 'fatal: cannot rebase with locally recorded submodule modifications'. No way to make the submodule clean without workarounds.

signals.topic: document-skills and example-skills plugins install identical 17 skills causing ~50k duplicate tokens in Claude Code context
signals.summary: Both the document-skills and example-skills plugins install the same 17 skills from the skills/ directory, wasting approximately 50k tokens of context (e.g., pptx skill alone is 6.3k tokens). Users installing both plugins — a reasonable choice given their distinct stated purposes — silently lose a significant portion of their context window.
aliases: duplicate skills plugin installation wastes tokens
signals.review_reason: Users who install both plugins (a reasonable choice given their different stated purposes) lose ~50k tokens of context to duplicate skill definitions. This directly impairs their ability to do useful work in Claude Code. The waste is automatic and non-obvious.

source_issues.title: document-skills and example-skills plugins install identical content, causing duplicate skills

signals.topic: File write operation repeatedly fails with path/argument parsing errors
signals.summary: Users encounter repeated file write failures where Goose's write tool returns 'Failed to parse arguments: missing field `path`' or cannot create files, causing task loops and inability to save generated code to disk.
signals.review_reason: Two independent users on different platforms (Windows, Chinese-speaking user) report file write/save failures that block the primary code-generation workflow. The repeated loop behavior in #8361 indicates a systematic failure, not a one-off misconfiguration. This is a core productivity feature being broken.

source_issues.title: 不能创建文件

source_issues.title: Can't write to file - Path error

signals.topic: Goose silently drops unmapped models from provider API responses, hiding OpenRouter and custom proxy models from the UI
signals.summary: Goose's fetch_recommended_models silently filters out any model not in its hardcoded CanonicalModelRegistry. This causes OpenRouter (hundreds of models), OmniRoute/LiteLLM custom proxies, and new models like claude-opus-4-6-thinking to be completely hidden from the UI dropdown, with no user-visible indication. Additionally, the 'dynamic_models: false' config field is defined but never actually used.
aliases: Model list filtering silently drops models
signals.review_reason: Two separate issues with the same root cause confirm this is a real architectural flaw. The impact is severe: users with valid API keys for OpenRouter or custom proxies cannot see or select the models they are paying for. This silently breaks the model selection experience for a broad set of providers without any user-visible error.

source_issues.title: Goose silently drops unmapped models from /v1/models, breaking OpenRouter, OmniRoute, and cutting off new models
source_issues.evidence: Two independent reports (#8321 and #8317) document the same root cause. #8321 shows OpenRouter hundreds of models silently hidden. #8317 shows custom provider 'dynamic_models: false' config is defined but never checked in the code — the API result always takes precedence. Code location identified in crates/goose/src/providers/base.rs and crates/goose/src/providers/openai.rs.

source_issues.title: Bug: dynamic_models field in custom provider config is ignored
source_issues.evidence: Custom provider configured with 'dynamic_models: false' and 2 static models still shows 500+ models from the API instead. The dynamic_models field exists in schema but is never checked in the actual instantiation or model-fetching logic.

signals.topic: Provider configuration failure shows hardcoded generic error message instead of actual provider error, blocking self-service diagnosis
signals.summary: When 'goose configure' fails during provider configuration (wrong model name, auth error, unsupported feature, network issue), the error dialog always shows the same hardcoded message 'Failed to configure provider: init chat completion request with tool did not succeed', completely hiding the real error. The actual error is briefly visible in the spinner before being overwritten.
aliases: Hardcoded error on provider setup failure
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports confirm the same diagnostic failure. The hardcoded error prevents all self-service troubleshooting during initial setup — a critical onboarding step. Users cannot distinguish between auth failures, wrong model names, missing features, or network issues.

source_issues.title: Provider config failure shows generic error instead of actual error message
source_issues.evidence: Windows user tried multiple setups (local model via sglang that didn't support tool calling, Groq model with wrong name) and received identical generic error for different root causes. Real error is visible briefly then overwritten.

source_issues.title: bug(cli): provider config failure shows generic error instead of actual error message
source_issues.evidence: Same bug reported independently. Confirms the hardcoded 'init chat completion request with tool did not succeed' message is shown regardless of the actual provider error (404, auth, network, unsupported feature).

signals.topic: iOS app stuck on session loading 85% of the time, blocking chat access
signals.summary: The iOS Goose app gets stuck on the session-loading screen the majority of the time after establishing a remote connection, making the mobile experience unusable for most interactions.
aliases: Mobile app stuck on session load
signals.review_reason: Although count=1, the 85% reproducible rate is strong user-impact evidence. The bug blocks the primary iOS chat interaction after a user has already completed the multi-step session setup. Tunnel connection is confirmed working, isolating this to the app's session-loading logic. High impact on mobile users.

source_issues.title: iOS app stuck on loading a session 85% of times
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly reports 85% failure rate — 'stuck on seesion-loading more often than not' with reproducible steps (macOS + iOS session pairing). Tunnel connection confirmed as 'ok', ruling out network cause.

signals.topic: Remote connection fails for non-localhost hosts due to self-signed cert rejection and CSP blocks plain HTTP
signals.summary: The Remote Connection feature cannot establish connections to external goosed servers on non-localhost hosts due to conflicting restrictions: self-signed certificates are rejected via certificate-error handler, and CSP blocks plain HTTP to non-localhost, creating a catch-22 where neither HTTPS nor HTTP works.
signals.review_reason: The Remote Connection feature is designed specifically for connecting to external goosed servers, yet it is entirely broken for non-localhost hosts. The user has a correctly configured remote server and secret key but faces an unrecoverable catch-22. This is a core feature being completely non-functional for its primary use case.

source_issues.title: Remote connection fails: self-signed cert rejected for non-localhost hosts + CSP blocks plain HTTP
source_issues.evidence: User has a valid remote goosed server with GOOSE_SERVER__SECRET_KEY, but Goose Desktop cannot connect due to conflicting security restrictions. The Remote Connection feature is entirely broken for the intended use case (external server).

signals.topic: Browser context destroyed (CDP session crash) when act() triggers window.print() PDF modal
signals.summary: Using act() to click a button that opens window.print() causes the CDP session to crash with 'Target page, context or browser has been closed'. The browser context becomes unusable after triggering the browser's native print dialog, blocking any subsequent CDP operations.
aliases: CDP session crash on PDF print modal
signals.review_reason: This is a real workflow-blocking bug: the browser context is destroyed when act() triggers window.print(), causing subsequent CDP operations to fail with TargetClosedError. This is a specific, reproducible failure path where a common user action (opening print dialog) renders the CDP session unusable, preventing the automation workflow from continuing. The issue has a clear error trace and a reproducible reproduction path.

source_issues.title: Opening Print PDF Modal on a tab with stagehand causes CDPSession.send: Target page, context or browser has been closed
source_issues.evidence: User clicks a button via act() that triggers window.print(); subsequent CDP operations fail with TargetClosedError: 'CDPSession.send: Target page, context or browser has been closed'. The CDP session is left in a dead state, making the browser automation workflow unusable after triggering the print dialog.

signals.topic: Gemini API quota (1m tokens/min) quickly exhausted during batch automation runs
signals.summary: Users running hundreds of Stagehand automation tasks in agent mode hit Gemini's 1m tokens/minute input quota limit rapidly, causing batch workflows to stall. The limit is not adjustable, leaving no workaround for large-scale automation.
aliases: Gemini rate limit blocking batch runs
Gemini token quota exhaustion during agent mode operations
signals.review_reason: This is a real rate-limiting pain point: users running batch automation workflows (100s of runs) quickly exhaust Gemini's non-adjustable 1m tokens/minute input quota, blocking large-scale automation. The issue is closed with no resolution, and the lack of a configurable quota means users cannot scale their workflows. This represents a significant operational blocker for power users.

source_issues.title: hitting gemini quota limits quickly, 1m tokens / minute
source_issues.evidence: User reports running '100s of runs, few at a time' in agent mode with caching enabled and hitting the Gemini 1m tokens/minute input quota limit. The quota is described as 'not adjustable past 1m/min', leaving the user with no workaround. 4 comments indicate this is a known pain point with community discussion.

signals.topic: act() variable interpolation failure: model inputs variable name placeholder instead of resolved value
signals.summary: When passing variables to act() (e.g., a password from environment), the model occasionally types the literal variable name (e.g., 'password') instead of the resolved variable value. This is an intermittent bug that causes credential/form data to be entered incorrectly.
aliases: Variable name instead of value in act()
Variable placeholder not resolved in act() input action
signals.review_reason: This is a real workflow bug causing incorrect data entry: when variables are passed to act(), the model sometimes substitutes the literal variable name instead of its resolved value. This has clear user impact (wrong form data/credentials entered) and is an intermittent but documented failure mode. While intermittent, it undermines trust in variable passing, a core feature for real-world automation use cases.

source_issues.title: Action with variables occasionally input variable name instead of variable values
source_issues.evidence: User passes a password variable to act() using a placeholder syntax (Type %password% into the password field), but the model sometimes inputs the literal string 'password' instead of the resolved variable value. This is a credential/credential-adjacent bug that causes incorrect form data entry. Issue is open with 1 comment and has been recently active.

signals.review_reason: 3 条独立 issue 均指向同一根因：recent update (#1931) 引入的 UUID 校验逻辑与 new 对话路由不兼容。核心主流程（新建对话后上传附件、发送消息）被完全阻断，是高发（count=3）+ 主流程阻断 + 有明确样例链接支撑的典型 P0 问题。

source_issues.title: #1931 更新出现的新bug:HTTP 422: {"detail":"Invalid thread ID: must be a UUID"}

signals.topic: Docker 部署后页面严重卡顿，多并发会话时前端直接卡死

signals.topic: R2 storage auto-save/backup not working despite correct configuration

signals.review_reason: Primary user interaction surface (chat UI) degrades significantly in routine long-conversation use. Even after the built-in compression workaround, the UI remains slow, indicating a real state management or rendering bug that impacts daily workflow.

source_issues.title: UI becomes extremely slow in long conversations
source_issues.evidence: User reports 500k+ token conversations cause slow chat loading, laggy settings menu, and slow conversation switching. Problem persists after compress feature is used, indicating a UI rendering/state management bug rather than a context size issue.

signals.topic: multi_edit: replying to chat without Accept/Reject causes model to assume edit succeeded, leading to cascading failures
signals.summary: When the multi_edit tool presents a diff and the user neither clicks Accept nor Reject but instead types a follow-up chat message, the tool call resolves with empty 'No tool output'. The model proceeds as if the edit was applied, then uses the (wrong) assumed-applied state for subsequent edit attempts, causing cascading failures.
signals.review_reason: This is a silent failure that corrupts the agent's internal model of file state, leading to cascading subsequent edit failures. The user gets no feedback that the edit was not applied, and the agent proceeds with incorrect assumptions, making iterative editing workflows unreliable.

source_issues.title: Replying to chat without clicking Accept or Reject on multi_edit produces 'No tool output'
source_issues.evidence: When user ignores the diff and types a chat reply, model receives empty tool output and assumes edit succeeded. Subsequent multi_edit calls use old_string values based on the assumed-applied edit, which no longer match actual file contents, causing them to fail. This is a silent, cascading workflow failure.

signals.review_reason: This is a clear experience regression: public documentation that users relied on for model configuration setup now requires authentication. source_issues.title: All model configuration pages (such as https://continue.dev/ollama/qwen2.5-coder-1.5b) redirect to an authentication page

signals.topic: IntelliJ: glob search without maxResults limit causes context overflow and workflow blockage in large repositories
signals.summary: The IntelliJ IDEA extension does not enforce the MAX_AGENT_GLOB_RESULTS limit (100) when executing glob searches. In repositories with 10k+ files, broad glob patterns (e.g., via @codebase) return the entire file list, immediately exhausting the context window and preventing any LLM interaction.
signals.review_reason: The @codebase context provider is completely broken for large repositories in IntelliJ, returning 10k+ items and causing 400 errors. This is a main-flow blockage for the IntelliJ user base working with real-world codebase sizes, rendering code-aware AI assistance unavailable.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Missing results limitation in IntelliJ getFileResults implementation causing context overflow
source_issues.evidence: Two-part root cause: (1) MessageIde class fails to forward maxResults to getFileResults request payload, (2) Kotlin getFileResults implementation doesn't truncate ripgrep output. Tested on 10k+ file repository; returns unfiltered list causing 400 Bad Request due to context length. The entire @codebase context provider is non-functional in large repos on IntelliJ.

signals.topic: AWS Bedrock LLM silently drops tool call arguments, causing TypeError/ValidationError
signals.summary: When using CrewAI with an AWS Bedrock LLM (e.g. Amazon Nova Pro), tool arguments are silently discarded. The LLM correctly calls the tool with arguments like {"city": "Paris"}, but the tool receives an empty dict {}, resulting in TypeError or Pydantic ValidationError.
aliases: tool call args silently dropped on Bedrock
Bedrock LLM tool input empty dict
signals.review_reason: Confirmed production bug in Bedrock LLM integration: tool arguments are silently discarded, causing TypeError or ValidationError at runtime. User's tool execution completely fails when using AWS Bedrock.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Bedrock tool call arguments silently dropped — tool invoked with empty input
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with reproduction steps. When Bedrock LLM calls a tool with correct arguments, tool receives {}. Confirmed in versions 1.9.3 and 1.13.0. Root cause traced to _extract_tool_call_info in crewai/agents/crew_agent_executor.py.

signals.topic: BrightData SERP tool uses JavaScript template literal syntax in Python f-strings, breaking all search queries
signals.summary: The get_search_url method in BrightDataSearchTool uses ${query} (JS template literal syntax) instead of {query} (Python f-string syntax), prepending a literal $ to every search query and producing broken URLs.
aliases: BrightData search URL JavaScript syntax bug
signals.review_reason: All BrightData SERP searches produce broken URLs (e.g. q=$AI%20news instead of q=AI%20news), making the entire tool non-functional for all three search engines. Clear production impact.

source_issues.title: [BUG] BrightData SERP tool uses JavaScript template syntax in Python f-strings, breaking all search queries
source_issues.evidence: Bug with exact code location (brightdata_serp.py lines 132-137). All three search engines (Google, Bing, Yandex) produce broken URLs with literal $ prefix. Python REPL evidence demonstrating the bug provided.

signals.topic: Regression in v1.11.1: Tool error handling and name collision resolution broken after PR #4656 fix was reverted
signals.summary: A cleanup commit (bb9bcd6) in v1.11.1 removed the _extract_tool_name() method that was added in PR #4656, causing tool error handling and name collision resolution to break. Tools with duplicate names may not be correctly distinguished.
signals.review_reason: Regression bug introduced in v1.11.1 that silently breaks core tool error handling and name collision resolution. The removed method was a fix from PR #4656. Users upgrading from v1.10.1 to v1.11.1 will experience silent tool failures.

source_issues.title: Regression: PR #4656 fix broken in v1.11.1 - Tool error handling and name collision resolution
source_issues.evidence: Regression documented with specific commit hash (bb9bcd6). _extract_tool_name() method removed as 'unused' but it was part of PR #4656 fix for tool error injection and name collision. Affects v1.10.1 (working) to v1.11.1 (broken).

signals.topic: Synchronous LLM call() blocks event loop in async workflows via converter/_export_output
signals.summary: In async workflows started via akickoff(), the converter module makes synchronous self.llm.call() invocations, blocking the event loop. This breaks async workflows when tasks use output_json or output_pydantic.
aliases: async workflow synchronous LLM call blocking event loop
converter sync call in async context
signals.review_reason: Async workflows using akickoff() with structured output (output_json/output_pydantic) make blocking synchronous LLM calls, causing event loop blocking. This breaks the core async execution model and can cause hangs or deadlocks in production async applications.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Do not invoke synchronous call() on LLM from asynchronous workflow in _export_output / converter
source_issues.evidence: Bug with exact file locations: converter.py and task.py lines. When async workflow uses output_json or output_pydantic, synchronous LLM.call() is invoked from _export_output, blocking the event loop. Traced to internal_instructor.py and converter.py.

signals.topic: InternalInstructor discards base_url for OpenAI-compatible endpoints — silently hits api.openai.com instead
signals.summary: When using OpenAI-compatible providers (vLLM, Ollama, self-hosted) with a custom base_url, InternalInstructor silently discards base_url and sends requests to api.openai.com, resulting in ConnectTimeout or ConverterError.
signals.review_reason: Silent endpoint misrouting for all OpenAI-compatible providers (vLLM, Ollama, etc.) using structured output. Users get ConnectTimeout or ConverterError with no indication that base_url was silently discarded. Common production setup pattern broken.

source_issues.title: [BUG] InternalInstructor discards base_url when creating instructor client — breaks OpenAI-compatible endpoints
source_issues.evidence: Bug with full code trace. InternalInstructor._create_instructor_client() extracts model name and provider but never forwards base_url. _get_llm_extra_kwargs() exists but guarded behind is_litellm=True. All structured output requests from OpenAI-compatible providers hit api.openai.com instead of configured endpoint.

signals.topic: Remote Ollama vendor configuration fails with 'could not find vendor' error despite correct .env setup
signals.summary: Users with correctly configured .env files (DEFAULT_VENDOR=Ollama, OLLAMA_API_URL, OLLAMA_BASE_URL) encounter 'could not find vendor' error when executing fabric commands, blocking the main workflow of querying Ollama models.
signals.review_reason: This is a workflow-blocking bug. The user has correctly configured the environment (env vars are confirmed set, 'fabric -L' successfully lists remote models), but the chat/stream execution path fails with a vendor mapping error. The CLI correctly reads the model name and vendor but cannot resolve it in the internal registry, causing the primary use case (querying Ollama) to fail entirely. It is not a one-off misconfiguration — the same pattern of 'could not find vendor' appears across multiple recent issues, indicating a systematic failure in vendor initialization/mapping for remote Ollama setups.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: 'could not find vendor' error despite correctly configured .env (Ollama/Remote)
source_issues.evidence: User correctly sets DEFAULT_VENDOR=Ollama and OLLAMA_API_URL/OLLAMA_BASE_URL in ~/.config/fabric/.env, but 'fabric --model ollama/huihui_ai/glm-4.7-flash-abliterated:latest --stream' returns 'could not find vendor'. Log output shows 'Default Vendor = Ollama.' but then 'could not find vendor', proving the config is read but vendor mapping fails.

signals.topic: Fabric server hangs indefinitely at Context= stage when connecting to remote Ollama provider (ECONNRESET)
signals.summary: When using fabric --serve with a remote Ollama instance, the server hangs at the Context= log stage and never returns tokens, eventually causing an ECONNRESET/socket hang up. The remote Ollama instance is reachable via curl and fabric -L, but the streaming handshake silently fails.
signals.review_reason: This blocks the server mode — a core feature for users wanting to host Fabric as an API. The server successfully receives and parses the request but the streaming connection to the remote Ollama provider silently fails, hanging until timeout. Since the remote Ollama is confirmed reachable, the failure is in the streaming handshake between Fabric's server and the Ollama API, making the entire server workflow unusable for remote setups.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Server hangs at Context= when using remote Ollama provider (ECONNRESET)
source_issues.evidence: Fabric server (--serve) correctly receives requests and identifies model/pattern, but hangs indefinitely at 'Processing prompt 1: Model=glm-4.7-flash:latest Pattern=extract_insights Context=' and never streams tokens. The hang eventually causes a socket hang up (ECONNRESET) in the Vite proxy. Remote Ollama is confirmed reachable via curl and fabric -L, and OLLAMA_ORIGINS='*' is set.

signals.topic: Enter key non-responsiveness and UI hang during option approval due to IDE connection fetch timeout
signals.summary: Multiple users report that the Enter key becomes intermittently non-responsive when approving options in the CLI, linked to an unhandled promise rejection in IDEConnectionUtils when a fetch to localhost MCP times out or fails. The UI rendering/input handling loop is blocked, halting the approval workflow.
aliases: Enter key unresponsive during tool confirmation
UI hang on IDE connection fetch timeout
signals.review_reason: Multiple users report Enter key non-responsiveness that blocks the core approval workflow. Stack trace shows a concrete unhandled promise rejection in IDEConnectionUtils linked to a localhost fetch timeout. The IDE connection failure propagates into the UI event loop, causing a functional block on the primary interaction path. High confidence from technical evidence.

source_issues.title: Intermittent 'Enter' key non-responsiveness and UI hang during option approval
source_issues.evidence: Stack trace shows unhandled promise rejection: UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT, fetch failed to http://127.0.0.1:38371/mcp. UI rendering/input loop blocked when IDEConnectionUtils fetch times out. Multiple users confirmed. Workaround: YOLO mode bypasses the problematic check.

signals.topic: JavaScript heap out of memory crash during long task execution
signals.summary: The CLI crashes with a fatal V8 heap out-of-memory error during long-running tasks, causing total workflow failure at ~90% task completion. Mark-Compact GC cycles repeatedly fail before the crash.
aliases: V8 heap out of memory crash
FATAL: Reached heap limit during long task
signals.review_reason: Total process termination with a complete V8 stack trace showing recursive JSON serialization causing heap exhaustion. Workflow failure at 90% completion is a severe user impact — the user's entire task is lost. The recursive JSON serialization loop in the stack trace provides a concrete root cause path.

source_issues.title: fata error
source_issues.evidence: FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory. Process crashes at ~90% task completion. Full V8 stack trace with recursive JSON serialization loop causing GC allocation failure.

signals.topic: Sandbox drops GOOGLE_GENAI_API_VERSION env var causing 404 ModelNotFoundError
signals.summary: When GEMINI_SANDBOX=true and GOOGLE_GENAI_API_VERSION are used together with GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL to form a Vertex API path, the sandbox silently drops the GOOGLE_GENAI_API_VERSION variable, resulting in an incomplete URL and a 404 ModelNotFoundError. The variable works outside the sandbox.
aliases: Sandbox 404 due to missing env var
GOOGLE_GENAI_API_VERSION not passed to sandbox container
signals.review_reason: Sandbox mode is completely broken for Vertex-compatible deployments when GOOGLE_GENAI_API_VERSION is required. Silent failure (404) with no user-facing explanation of the root cause. Clear regression: the env var was added in a recent PR but the corresponding sandbox.ts update was missed. The workaround is a hidden escape hatch that most users won't find.

source_issues.title: Sandbox does not forward GOOGLE_GENAI_API_VERSION into container
source_issues.evidence: ModelNotFoundError: Not found (404) when GEMINI_SANDBOX=true with GOOGLE_GENAI_API_VERSION and GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL. sandbox.ts forwards other GOOGLE_* vars but was not updated when GOOGLE_GENAI_API_VERSION support was added. Unsetting GEMINI_SANDBOX makes it work. Workaround via SANDBOX_ENV escape hatch exists but is undocumented.

signals.topic: CLI displays misleading 'API key expired' error when key is actually invalid
signals.summary: The CLI returns a misleading error message stating the API key has expired when the actual problem is that the key is invalid (INVALID_ARGUMENT / API_KEY_INVALID). This misleads users into trying to renew a key that may be valid but misconfigured, delaying correct diagnosis.
aliases: API key invalid vs expired confusion
signals.review_reason: Misleading error message is a clear UX/communication defect. While the underlying issue may be user configuration, displaying 'expired' when the key is 'invalid' causes users to pursue the wrong remediation path, representing a direct user experience harm. The error mapping is incorrect.

source_issues.title: Getting API key expired. Please renew the API key error
source_issues.evidence: Error body shows 'API_KEY_INVALID' reason and 'API key expired' message. The API returns INVALID_ARGUMENT with API_KEY_INVALID domain, but the CLI surfaces this as a misleading 'key expired' message. User is misled about root cause.

signals.topic: Windows symlink permission error (EPERM) prevents skills from being linked
signals.summary: On Windows 10, the skills linking operation fails with EPERM (operation not permitted) when trying to create symlinks, blocking users from setting up skills. The Node.js process lacks filesystem permissions needed for the symlink operation on Windows.
aliases: Windows EPERM symlink error skills setup
Permission denied on skill symlink Windows
signals.review_reason: Skills linking is a core setup workflow that is blocked entirely on Windows due to symlink permissions. This is a platform-critical regression that prevents the skills feature from functioning on Windows, a major desktop platform. Clear OS-level permission error with concrete impact on feature availability.

source_issues.title: Permission error with skills linking on Windows 10
source_issues.evidence: EPERM: operation not permitted, symlink operation fails on Windows 10 during skills linking. Gemini CLI 0.36.0 on win32. Blocking skills setup on Windows, a major platform.

signals.topic: Multi-agent sub-agent failures return silent None/empty results, causing manager loops or hallucinations
signals.summary: When sub-agents fail (tool error or max_steps exceeded) in a ManagedAgent multi-agent setup, the manager receives None/empty instead of an error signal. Manager cannot distinguish 'task completed with empty output' from 'task failed', leading to retry loops or fabricated results.
aliases: silent sub-agent failure in multi-agent pipelines
ManagedAgent returns None on sub-agent failure
signals.review_reason: This is a production-breaking bug in multi-agent workflows: sub-agents silently fail and return None/empty, leaving the manager with no error signal. The manager either retries in a loop or proceeds with hallucinations — both outcomes are severe for production deployments. Issue #2166 provides a reproducible code example with LiteLLMModel, explicitly describes the mechanism (ManagedAgent.__call__ returning empty/None), and identifies the root cause location. The severity is high because multi-agent orchestration is a core use case and silent failures at sub-agent boundaries are undetectable without instrumentation.

source_issues.title: ManagedAgent swallows tool errors from sub-agents - manager sees empty/None result
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible with CodeAgent+LiteLLMModel+ManagedAgent. Sub-agent with empty tools and max_steps=2 returns '' or None to manager. Manager may then hallucinate a result or loop indefinitely. Author explicitly states this is one of the hardest categories to debug in production multi-agent pipelines.

signals.topic: MultiStepAgent has no built-in retry for transient model API errors, causing entire multi-step runs to fail and lose progress
signals.summary: When a model API call (rate limit 429, 503, timeout) fails inside MultiStepAgent.run(), the entire agent run fails immediately with no retry. For long multi-step tasks (e.g., step 8 of 10), this means the entire run is lost and must be restarted from scratch, wasting compute and developer time.
aliases: No retry/backoff for transient API errors
rate limit crashes entire agent run
signals.review_reason: This is a primary workflow failure: transient model errors (429, 503, timeout) crash entire multi-step agent runs with no retry, losing all prior progress. For production agents handling multi-step tasks, this causes repeated work loss, wasted API calls, and manual restarts. Issue #2165 provides a concrete reproduction with LiteLLMModel, specifies which HTTP codes are retryable (429, 500, 502, 503, 504), identifies that litellm's own retry support is inconsistent across providers making an agent-level layer necessary, and documents the workaround (custom model wrapper) as non-obvious and duplicated. The P0 rating is justified because step 8 of 10 failure losing 7 steps of context is a direct, reproducible workflow blocker with no in-library solution.

source_issues.title: No built-in retry/backoff for transient model API errors in MultiStepAgent
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible with LiteLLMModel. Step 8 of a 10-step task hitting a 429 raises immediately, losing all prior 7 steps of work. Users must implement custom model wrappers with retry logic, which is non-obvious and duplicated per project. Author explicitly calls out litellm retry support as inconsistent across providers, making an agent-level retry layer necessary for all backends.

signals.topic: VisitWebpageTool has no response size limit, silently overflowing context windows and causing agent failures
signals.summary: VisitWebpageTool fetches full page text without any size cap. On large pages (SEC filings, Wikipedia, documentation), it returns hundreds of KB of text in a single tool call, silently overflowing the model's context window. The agent receives no error — it either gets a truncated result or fails at the API level with a misleading context-length error that appears to be an LLM bug rather than a tool bug.
aliases: large page content overflows context window
signals.review_reason: This is a critical tool usability failure: VisitWebpageTool silently overflows context windows on large pages, causing agent failures that are misdiagnosed as LLM bugs rather than tool bugs. The confusion is compounded because the failure is silent (no tool error) and the API error message points to the LLM rather than the tool. Issue #2164 provides a reproducible example, notes that DuckDuckGoSearchTool already implements size capping (proving the expected behavior), and correctly identifies the root cause as a missing truncation step in the tool. Closed state likely indicates a fix was applied, but the issue serves as documented evidence of a real, diagnosed user impact that required a library change.

source_issues.title: VisitWebpageTool has no response size limit and can silently overflow context window
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible with HfApiModel and VisitWebpageTool visiting large pages (Wikipedia). Tool returns ~80KB+ of text silently overflowing context window. The failure manifests as a misleading API-level context error rather than a tool error, making root cause diagnosis difficult. Author notes DuckDuckGoSearchTool already has max_results for size capping — same pattern should apply. Issue was closed (likely with a fix) but the underlying pattern remains a validated user impact issue.

signals.topic: WebSearchTool hardcodes HTTP timeout to 30s with no user-configurable override, breaking in diverse network environments
signals.summary: All three WebSearchTool backends (Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo) hardcode timeout=30 in requests.get calls, and the Exa backend added in PR #2139 has no timeout at all. Users in corporate proxies or slow networks face unavoidable ReadTimeout errors. Users requiring low-latency agents cannot reduce the timeout. No workaround exists without subclassing or monkey-patching.
aliases: no configurable HTTP timeout in search tool
signals.review_reason: This is a real production environment incompatibility: WebSearchTool's hardcoded 30-second timeout causes ReadTimeout failures in legitimate corporate proxy/slow network scenarios, aborting agent runs with no user-configurable override. Two distinct failure modes are documented (slow networks timeout, low-latency apps wait too long), and the issue traces back to two specific PRs (#2139, #2140) confirming the pattern was introduced without configurability. Downgraded to P2 because it does not block the primary agent workflow — it is an environment-specific degradation rather than a universal failure — but it is retained as a valid pain point since there is no workaround without modifying library internals.

source_issues.title: Make HTTP request timeout configurable in WebSearchTool
source_issues.evidence: Author identifies two real-world failure scenarios: (1) corporate proxies/slow networks where legitimate requests exceed 30s causing avoidable ReadTimeout that aborts agent runs; (2) latency-sensitive streaming/realtime apps where 30s is far too long. No workaround without subclassing or monkey-patching. Issue also notes the Exa backend added no timeout at all, creating an additional inconsistency. Traced back to PR #2139 and PR #2140, confirming the hardcoded value was added intentionally but without configurability.

signals.topic: Agent can train on holdout/test data due to data loading design flaw
signals.summary: load_data() returns full dataset including holdout sales, allowing the agent to train directly on test data and achieve artificially zero error (WAPE=0.0000). Fix required adding an internal holdout split inside evaluate(). Root cause: immutable by instruction is not sufficient; data separation must be enforced by design.
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user-impacting data integrity flaw: the agent can (and did) train on holdout data, producing meaningless zero-error results that corrupt the entire research loop. The issue directly demonstrates real impact (WAPE=0.0000 exploit), not just theoretical risk. While count=1, the pattern of 'evaluators find loopholes humans don't anticipate' is a systemic design problem in autonomous evaluation loops, consistent with published research (arXiv:2408.07678). The root cause is an architectural design flaw: data separation is not enforced by design, only by instruction.

source_issues.title: Applied autoresearch to Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM) — 12x improvement, beat Google Meridian
source_issues.evidence: Agent discovered that load_data() returned full dataset including holdout sales. It trained OLS directly on test data → WAPE = 0.0000 (artificially perfect). This was a valid evaluation loophole found autonomously. Research results would be completely meaningless if not caught and fixed.

signals.topic: Codex ignores 'never stop' instruction and stops prematurely in interactive sessions
signals.summary: Codex-based interactive sessions do not honor the 'never stop' behavior required for autonomous research loops, unlike Claude which works correctly. This breaks the core interactive autonomous workflow for users who prefer or need Codex.
signals.review_reason: This is a user-impacting workflow break: Codex users cannot use the core interactive autonomous research loop. The original repo owner filed this issue, confirming it's a real blocker. 36 comments indicate broad community impact. The alternative (ralph loop) is explicitly worse — non-interactive sessions mean users lose visibility into what the agent is doing. While count=1, the impact is clearly blocking for the entire Codex user segment of autoresearch users.

source_issues.title: Codex doesn't seem to work?
source_issues.evidence: Original author (karpathy) reports Codex ignores instruction to never stop, breaking the interactive autonomous loop. 36 comments indicate sustained community interest. Users who prefer Codex cannot use autoresearch interactively — they are forced to use non-interactive ralph loop instead, losing visibility into agent progress.

signals.topic: RunloopSandbox batch file operations crash on single file failure — no per-file error handling
signals.summary: download_files() and upload_files() in RunloopSandbox throw uncaught exceptions on any single-file failure (e.g. file-not-found, permission denied), crashing the entire batch and returning raw SDK exceptions instead of partial results.
aliases: download_files crashes on file not found
signals.review_reason: Two external bug reports confirm that download_files/upload_files have no per-file exception handling. A single file failure (not-found, permission denied) raises uncaught exception, aborting the entire batch. This is a clear workflow-blocking issue with partial-success semantics violation.

source_issues.title: RunloopSandbox.download_files and upload_files lack per-file error handling — single failure crashes entire batch
source_issues.evidence: External bug report. download_files/upload_files catch no per-file exceptions; a single file error aborts entire batch with raw SDK exception. Contradicts BaseSandbox protocol which requires partial-success semantics.

source_issues.title: bug(runloop): download_files and upload_files lack per-file error handling — single failure crashes entire batch
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate external bug report of #2507. Same per-file error handling gap causes entire batch to abort on first failure.

signals.topic: Playwright browser tool calls are cancelled before completion — browser automation blocked
signals.summary: playwright_browser_navigate tool calls are frequently cancelled with 'another message came in before it could be completed', preventing all browser automation, web scraping, and UI testing workflows.
signals.review_reason: Two external bug reports confirm that playwright_browser_navigate tool calls are repeatedly cancelled before completion. This is not a transient issue — it blocks all browser automation, web scraping, and UI testing use cases, representing critical functionality unavailability.

source_issues.title: Playwright Browser Tool Call Cancellation Error
source_issues.evidence: External bug report with reproducible steps and error message: 'Tool call playwright_browser_navigate with id ... was cancelled - another message came in before it could be completed.' Prevents browser automation tasks entirely.

source_issues.title: Playwright Browser Tool Call Cancellation Error
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate external bug report. Same cancellation error pattern for playwright_browser_navigate. Impact: browser automation, web scraping, and UI testing workflows all blocked.

signals.topic: FilesystemMiddleware drops goto and graph fields from Command objects — workflow routing silently fails
signals.summary: FilesystemMiddleware._intercept_large_tool_result extracts text from Command objects but discards the 'goto' and 'graph' routing fields, causing parent-agent routing logic to silently break when large file results are intercepted.
aliases: Command routing fields dropped by FilesystemMiddleware
parent agent routing fails after large file result
signals.review_reason: External bug report with reproduction code confirms FilesystemMiddleware silently drops goto/graph fields from Command objects during large result interception. This causes parent-agent routing to silently fail — agents intended to transfer to specific sub-agents instead continue default execution. Low frequency (count=1) but the impact is a silent workflow routing failure.

source_issues.title: FilesystemMiddleware._intercept_large_tool_result drops goto and graph from Command objects
source_issues.evidence: External bug report with reproduction code. FilesystemMiddleware._intercept_large_tool_result extracts text but drops Command.goto and Command.graph fields, causing parent-agent routing to silently fail. Explicitly shows Command with goto='agent_b' losing routing behavior.

signals.topic: CLI non-interactive mode has contradictory todo instructions — agent behavior undefined
signals.summary: In non-interactive CLI mode the system prompt simultaneously says 'Do NOT ask clarifying questions / proceed alone' and 'Wait for the user's response before marking the first todo', causing contradictory agent behavior.
signals.review_reason: External bug report with executable reproduction confirms the non-interactive CLI prompt contains directly contradictory instructions — must not ask user but must wait for user before marking todos. This creates undefined agent behavior in headless/CI environments where the CLI is commonly used.

source_issues.title: Conflicting instructions for todos in non-interactive mode in CLI
source_issues.evidence: External bug report with assertion-based reproduction. Prompt contains both 'Do NOT ask clarifying questions' (headless policy) and 'Wait for the user's response before marking the first todo' (interactive policy) — directly contradictory instructions in a single system prompt for non-interactive mode.

signals.topic: deepagents-cli installation requires langsmith[sandbox] causing websockets version conflict — install blocked
signals.summary: pip install deepagents-cli pulls in langsmith[sandbox] which pins websockets<16, causing installation to fail in environments requiring websockets>=16.
aliases: pip install deepagents-cli fails due to websockets constraint
signals.review_reason: External bug report confirms installation of deepagents-cli is blocked in any environment that requires websockets>=16 due to a transitive dependency pinning websockets<16. This is a hard installation block that prevents the entire CLI from being used in affected environments, which meets the bar for P1 even at count=1 due to the severity of complete unavailability.

source_issues.title: Make LangSmith sandbox optional in deepagents-cli to avoid websockets conflicts
source_issues.evidence: External bug report. Installing deepagents-cli pulls langsmith[sandbox] which pins websockets<16. Environments requiring websockets>=16 cannot install the CLI at all — hard installation block with no workaround for users in affected environments.

signals.topic: Ollama: reasoning_content suppressed and message mutation causing tool call failures
signals.summary: Three related Ollama integration bugs that collectively block agentic tool-use: reasoning output silently suppressed when bind_tools() is used with large prompts, caller list mutated in-place corrupting multi-turn conversation history, and tool call parsing fails with Go unmarshal error.
signals.review_reason: Three distinct but related Ollama issues that collectively block agentic tool-use workflows: reasoning output is silently suppressed when bind_tools() is used with large prompts (key feature of reasoning models broken), caller list is silently mutated corrupting conversation history in multi-turn chats, and tool call parsing fails entirely with a Go unmarshal error. Count=3 meets P0 threshold with explicit blocking evidence.

source_issues.title: `ChatOllama.bind_tools()` with large system prompt suppresses reasoning output on `gemma4:26b`
source_issues.evidence: When reasoning=True and bind_tools() with complex schema + large system prompt (~2-3k tokens), gemma4:26b stops emitting reasoning_content in streamed chunks entirely, breaking key reasoning model workflows

source_issues.title: fix(ollama): `_convert_messages_to_ollama_messages` mutates caller's list in-place
source_issues.evidence: Function silently replaces elements in the caller's original list when encountering AIMessage with output_version==v1, causing data corruption in multi-turn agent conversations

source_issues.title: `cannot unmarshal array into Go value of type api.ToolCallFunctionArguments (status code: -1)`
