signals.topic: with_structured_output() crashes/warnings across Pydantic serialization, RunnableWithFallbacks, and ChatBedrockConverse
signals.summary: Core with_structured_output() API breaks in three different components: regression causes unexpected Pydantic serialization warnings (data may be silently corrupted), RunnableWithFallbacks crashes with NameError on forward-ref schemas, and ChatBedrockConverse crashes on function_call blocks in fallback chains.
signals.review_reason: Three different components all fail on with_structured_output() — a core API. Issue 36589 shows regression from 0.3.28 to 1.1.0 causing unexpected serialization behavior that silently corrupts output data. Issue 36579 causes a full crash (NameError) when wrapping runnables with structured output schemas using forward refs. Issue 36531 causes ValueError crash in multi-model fallback chains. All three directly break the main structured-output workflow users rely on.

source_issues.title: After recent langchain update, many pydantic serialization warnings
source_issues.evidence: with_structured_output() produces PydanticSerializationUnexpectedValue warnings after updating to v1.1.0 that did not exist in 0.3.28, indicating silent data transformation that may corrupt structured outputs

source_issues.title: RunnableWithFallbacks.__getattr__ raises NameError on methods with unresolvable forward-ref annotations
source_issues.evidence: with_structured_output(schema) on RunnableWithFallbacks crashes with NameError: name 'Runnable' is not defined when typing.get_type_hints encounters unresolvable forward refs, blocking structured output entirely for wrapped runnables

source_issues.title: ChatBedrockConverse crashes on function_call content blocks from OpenAI Responses API when used with ModelFallbackMiddleware
source_issues.evidence: ValueError: Unsupported content block type when ModelFallbackMiddleware passes AzureChatOpenAI Responses API history to ChatBedrockConverse; crashes on function_call blocks that the converter doesn't handle, blocking fallback chains entirely

signals.topic: ChatOpenRouter default_headers silently absorbed and wrap_model_call ToolStrategy narrowing not enforced
signals.summary: Two bugs cause documented features to silently not work: ChatOpenRouter absorbs HTTP headers into request body instead of sending them, blocking xAI prompt caching (45.9pp cache hit rate loss); wrap_model_call middleware's ToolStrategy narrowing is validated but never enforced at runtime, leaving all tools bound.
signals.review_reason: Issue 36581 causes ChatOpenRouter to silently corrupt header injection — HTTP headers end up in the request body instead of being sent as actual HTTP headers, blocking xAI prompt caching which the user explicitly documents as providing a 45.9pp higher cache hit rate (significant cost savings). Issue 36568 makes wrap_model_call middleware ToolStrategy narrowing ineffective — the API claims to support runtime narrowing of tools but the narrowing is only validated, never enforced. Both prevent documented features from working correctly.

source_issues.title: `ChatOpenRouter` silently swallows `default_headers`
source_issues.evidence: default_headers parameter is silently absorbed into model_kwargs with a misleading warning, causing HTTP headers to be serialized into the request body instead. This blocks xAI's x-grok-conv-id header needed for prompt caching, which shows a 45.9 percentage point improvement in cache hit rate. Cost and performance impact is clearly documented.

source_issues.title: `wrap_model_call` middleware ToolStrategy narrowing has no effect — model still sees all structured output tools
source_issues.evidence: request.override(response_format=ToolStrategy(SubsetType)) is validated but never actually enforced. All structured output tools from the original union remain bound to the model at runtime, defeating the purpose of ToolStrategy narrowing for cost and token optimization.

signals.topic: RuntimeError blocking LangGraph Cloud executor workflow due to execution_info patching failure
signals.summary: Users deploying to LangGraph Cloud encounter a RuntimeError when the framework cannot patch execution_info before it has been set, blocking the executor workflow. 8 comments indicate active discussion and a confirmed regression in version 0.7.96.
aliases: execution_info patch failure on cloud executor
signals.review_reason: Confirmed regression in LangGraph Cloud executor (0.7.96) causing a RuntimeError that blocks workflow execution. Active discussion with 8 comments confirms real user impact. Production environment blocking.

source_issues.title: RuntimeError: Cannot patch execution_info before it has been set on LangGraph Cloud executor 0.7.96
source_issues.evidence: Labeled as bug, 8 comments, confirmed regression in 0.7.96 on LangGraph Cloud executor, directly blocks workflow execution on cloud platform.

signals.topic: Long-running tool calls (180s+) silently re-executed from checkpoint on LangGraph Cloud causing duplicate execution and wasted compute cost
signals.summary: When a tool call exceeds ~3 minutes on LangGraph Cloud, it is silently re-dispatched from the last checkpoint while the original is still running, causing duplicate executions, wasted compute cost, and potential data inconsistency.
aliases: silent tool re-execution on LangGraph Cloud
duplicate tool calls from checkpoint timeout
tool call duplication after 180 seconds cloud
signals.review_reason: Silent duplicate execution of long-running tool calls (180s+) on LangGraph Cloud. This causes wasted compute cost and data inconsistency — real production impact. Issue #7213 was marked as duplicate of this one, confirming it affects multiple reports.

source_issues.title: Long tool calls (~180s+) silently re-executed from checkpoint on LangGraph Cloud
source_issues.evidence: Clear user-reported behavior: long-running tool calls are silently re-dispatched from checkpoint while original is still running, causing duplicate executions and wasted compute cost on LangGraph Cloud.

signals.topic: Default handle_tool_errors fails to catch execution errors in parallel tool calls in ToolNode prebuilt
signals.summary: When ToolNode executes multiple tool calls in parallel using asyncio.gather or executor.map, the default error handler only catches ToolInvocationError but not raw tool execution errors, causing unhandled exceptions in parallel tool call scenarios.
aliases: parallel tool call error handler bypass
signals.review_reason: Prebuilt ToolNode's default error handler bypass in parallel tool calls causes unhandled exceptions. This affects any user using async or sync parallel tool execution, a common production pattern.

source_issues.title: fix(prebuilt): Default handle_tool_errors doesn't catch tool execution errors in parallel calls
source_issues.evidence: Bug in prebuilt ToolNode: parallel tool calls via asyncio.gather/executor.map bypass the default error handler because only ToolInvocationError is caught, not raw execution errors. 1 comment confirming the fix approach.

signals.topic: langgraph-prebuilt version incompatibility with older langgraph versions causing ImportError at runtime
signals.summary: Updating langgraph-prebuilt to v1.0.9 breaks compatibility with older langgraph versions, causing 'Cannot import name ServerInfo from langgraph.runtime' ImportError. Users who update prebuilt independently cannot run their existing code.
signals.review_reason: Version incompatibility between langgraph-prebuilt and langgraph causes ImportError at runtime, fully blocking applications. 8 comments indicate widespread user impact. This is a classic breaking change across co-released packages.

source_issues.title: langgraph-prebuilt v1.0.9 breaks with older versions of langgraph. Cannot import name 'ServerInfo' from 'langgraph.runtime'
source_issues.evidence: Labeled as bug with 8 comments. Updating prebuilt independently causes ImportError at runtime, blocking user's application from starting. Version pinning problem between two packages from the same ecosystem.

signals.topic: InvalidNamespaceError when namespace contains mixed-type labels (int and str) in langgraph.store
signals.summary: langgraph.store.base raises InvalidNamespaceError when namespace labels are mixed (e.g., ('rag-agent', 1, 'rag-agent')), requiring all labels to be strings. This is a data model constraint mismatch that breaks common usage patterns.
aliases: mixed int str namespace labels store
signals.review_reason: Store API constraint that rejects mixed-type namespace labels causes runtime InvalidNamespaceError. Common usage pattern (passing integer IDs in namespaces) is broken. Labeled bug with confirmed error behavior.

source_issues.title: langgraph.store.base.InvalidNamespaceError: Invalid namespace label '1' found in ('rag-agent', 1, 'rag-agent'). Namespace labels must be strings, but got int.
source_issues.evidence: Labeled as bug with 1 comment. Store API rejects mixed-type namespace labels, causing InvalidNamespaceError at runtime for users who pass integers in namespace tuples.

signals.topic: Workflow WebApp Human Input flow: UI stuck in loading state after resume and no copy action for multi-output results
signals.summary: Public Workflow WebApp containing a Human Input node has two related issues after human input is submitted: (1) UI remains in loading/spinning state even though the backend workflow run has succeeded, never transitioning to completed state; (2) no usable copy action for multi-output workflow results. Both block the human-in-the-loop workflow completion UX.
aliases: Human Input node webapp stuck loading
workflow webapp copy action missing for multi-output
signals.review_reason: Two separate issues on the same app type (public Workflow WebApp with Human Input node) share the same root cause: missing state transition handling for NodeRunHumanInputFormFilledEvent and missing copy action for multi-field outputs. Both directly prevent users from completing a human-in-the-loop workflow — #34631 is blocking (UI stuck in loading forever after input resume), #34632 is a UX degradation (no way to copy structured results). Count=2 meets threshold. These are not the same bug as the previously-fixed #32649 (copy button for single output).

source_issues.title: Public Workflow WebApp remains loading after Human Input resume although workflow run succeeded
source_issues.evidence: Backend workflow run status=succeeded, workflow_pauses record removed, API returns 200, but public WebApp UI keeps spinning/loading. Worker log shows: 'Unhandled event type: NodeRunHumanInputFormFilledEvent'. UI never reaches completed state, result actions unusable.

source_issues.title: Published Workflow WebApp has no usable copy action for multi-output workflow results
source_issues.evidence: Workflow app with End node outputting multiple fields (confirmed_rules, master_json, layer2_json) published as public WebApp — no copy action available for results. User cannot copy multi-field output from published WebApp.

signals.topic: Datasets page throws 'embeddings is not a valid ModelType' error, blocking dataset access
signals.summary: Entering the datasets page triggers a validation error: 'embeddings' is not a valid ModelType. This is a main-flow blocker — users cannot access the datasets feature at all.
aliases: ModelType validation error on datasets page
embeddings ModelType error blocking dataset access
signals.review_reason: Even though count=1, this is a main-flow blocker. The datasets feature is core to Dify's RAG capability and is completely inaccessible when this error occurs. User clearly describes the failure path and the UI error is explicitly shown. The bug is labeled '🐞 bug' and has a comment suggesting active investigation.

source_issues.title: embeddings' is not a valid ModelType
source_issues.evidence: User enters datasets page on v1.13.3 self-hosted and immediately gets error 'embeddings' is not a valid ModelType. Main feature (datasets) becomes inaccessible. One comment on issue suggests a potential code path.

signals.topic: Knowledge pipeline template service returns 404, making template creation feature unavailable
signals.summary: The official Dify template service (tmpl.dify.ai/pipeline-templates) returns HTTP 404, causing the knowledge pipeline template list to display blank. Users cannot browse or select official pipeline templates when creating knowledge pipelines.
signals.review_reason: A Dify-owned external service (tmpl.dify.ai) is returning 404, making a core feature (pipeline template selection) completely unavailable. User impact is clear: blank template list. The issue references two prior incidents (#29769, #29209) suggesting this is a recurring service availability problem, not a one-off. The Chinese locale also exposes a JSON parse error from the same endpoint.

source_issues.title: knowledge pipeline template service is unavailable
source_issues.evidence: User navigates to Knowledge -> create from knowledge pipeline and sees no default templates. API log shows: GET https://tmpl.dify.ai/pipeline-templates?language=en-US HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found. System falls back to empty database. Related to prior incidents #29769 and #29209 indicating this is a recurring problem. Chinese locale shows JSON parse error at char 576206 suggesting a malformed response being served.

signals.topic: Chatflow publishing fails with error after adding skill, blocking workflow deployment
signals.summary: After adding a skill in Chatflow, publishing the workflow fails with an error. Users cannot deploy Chatflow apps that use skills.
aliases: workflow deployment fails on skill addition
signals.review_reason: Workflow publishing is a main workflow action that fails unconditionally when a skill is added. This blocks the entire deployment flow for Chatflow apps using skills. Screenshot evidence provided. The failure is reproducible and clearly blocks the user from using the skill feature in production.

source_issues.title: Chatflow publishing failed
source_issues.evidence: User adds a skill in Chatflow and attempts to publish, triggering an error shown in the UI. Screenshot of error message attached. One comment indicates active discussion. Version 1.14.0-rc1.

signals.topic: Chatflow streaming breaks and messages disappear on browser tab switch
signals.summary: During a Chatflow streaming response, if the user switches to another browser tab, the stream halts and the last sent message (both user input and LLM streaming response) disappears. Reloading the page is required to see results.
aliases: Streaming message loss on tab switch
ChatFlow stream broken by browser tab change
signals.review_reason: This causes data loss during active use — both user input and partial LLM response disappear on tab switch. This is a significant UX degradation that affects every user who has any workflow running in a browser tab and switches tabs (a common behavior). The user's input is lost, which is a clear user impact beyond mere inconvenience.

source_issues.title: User Input and ChatFlow history messages (last message that been streaming) disappears on tab change while streaming
source_issues.evidence: User sends a message in ChatFlow and switches browser tabs before the LLM response completes. Upon returning, both the user input and the streaming LLM response are gone. User must reload to see any result. Explicitly noted as a 'major UX problem' as users commonly switch tabs while waiting for responses.

signals.topic: Ollama embedding endpoint mismatch — plugin uses wrong path /v1/embeddings instead of /api/embeddings, causing TypeError: fetch failed
signals.summary: When mem0 plugin is configured with Ollama as embedder provider, it incorrectly calls the OpenAI-style /v1/embeddings endpoint instead of Ollama's required /api/embeddings. This causes all embedding lookups to fail with 'TypeError: fetch failed', making memory search and auto-capture completely non-functional for Ollama users.
signals.review_reason: This is a primary-flow blocker: embedding lookup is the foundational operation for all memory search and capture in OSS mode. Without embeddings working, the entire memory system is non-functional. Two independent issue reports confirm the same root cause (wrong endpoint path for Ollama) and a related dimension mismatch issue, both of which block the core memory pipeline.

source_issues.title: mem0 plugin fails with "TypeError: fetch failed" when using Ollama – wrong embeddings endpoint (/v1/embeddings)
source_issues.evidence: Mem0 plugin attempts to call POST http://192.168.110.14:11434/v1/embeddings which Ollama does not expose. Should call /api/embeddings. Error: TypeError: fetch failed. All search operations fail.

source_issues.title: Ollama embedding dimensions not propagated to Qdrant vector store (bge-m3: 1024 vs hardcoded 1536)
source_issues.evidence: bge-m3 (1024 dims) and nomic-embed-text (768 dims) produce wrong-dimension embeddings due to hardcoded 1536 default in Qdrant store. Embedding dims from Ollama config not propagated to vector store, causing dimension mismatch errors.

signals.topic: OpenClaw pgvector OSS mode — 'Client has already been connected' crash preventing all memory operations
signals.summary: In OpenClaw OSS mode with pgvector configured, the pg client is reused across connections, causing 'Client has already been connected. You cannot reuse a client' errors. Memory initialization fails, recall times out, and all subsequent memory operations (recall, capture) crash repeatedly.
signals.review_reason: This is a complete functional breakdown for OSS users choosing pgvector as their vector store. Every memory operation fails (initialization, recall, capture), making the pgvector OSS configuration completely unusable. The error is repeatable, has clear stack traces showing the pg client reuse bug in PGVector.initialize, and affects a core integration path.

source_issues.title: [Bug][OpenClaw][OSS/pgvector] openclaw-mem0 crashes/fails when using pgvector in OSS mode
source_issues.evidence: Error: Client has already been connected. You cannot reuse a client. at PGVector.initialize. This error repeats across all memory operations: recall timed out after 8000ms, initialization fails repeatedly, capture fails. Complete breakdown of OSS memory functionality with pgvector.

signals.topic: LLM config ignores user-provided url field — TypeScript SDK sends requests to api.openai.com instead of configured provider (Ollama, etc.)
signals.summary: The TypeScript SDK ConfigManager.mergeConfig() for LLM does not fall back to userConf.url, silently ignoring user-provided custom LLM URLs. Requests go to api.openai.com instead, causing either TypeError: fetch failed (if no internet), 404 errors, or silently routing to the wrong host.
aliases: TypeScript SDK LLM baseURL fallback broken
LLM url config ignored TS SDK
signals.review_reason: A silent misrouting bug where configured LLM endpoints are completely ignored, causing all LLM calls to go to OpenAI instead. This is a primary-flow blocker for any TypeScript SDK user using non-OpenAI LLM providers (Ollama, custom endpoints, etc.). The bug is confirmed by code comparison showing url fallback is implemented for embedder config but missing for LLM config.

source_issues.title: LLM config manager ignores url field — Ollama/custom LLM providers connect to api.openai.com
source_issues.evidence: When configuring Ollama with url: 'http://my-ollama-host:11434', LLM config manager ignores it and uses https://api.openai.com/v1. Results in: TypeError: fetch failed (no internet path), 404 (wrong host), or silent wrong-host routing. Root cause: LLM config skips userConf.url in fallback chain unlike embedder config.

signals.topic: OpenAI-compatible providers broken by unconditional store=False field — Gemini and other non-OpenAI backends reject the parameter
signals.summary: OpenAIConfig defaults store=False, and generate_response() unconditionally sends 'store': False to all OpenAI-compatible backends via hasattr checks. Gemini and other non-OpenAI providers that don't recognize the 'store' field reject the request, breaking all memory operations.
aliases: OpenAI-specific params leaked to compatible backends
signals.review_reason: This breaks the core add() operation for any non-OpenAI provider using the OpenAI-compatible API — a very common deployment pattern. Gemini, Groq, Mistral, and local proxies are all affected. The workaround requires monkey-patching the SDK, which is unacceptable for production use. Clear code-path evidence confirms the root cause.

source_issues.title: [Bug][Python] store=False unconditionally sent to all OpenAI-compatible backends — breaks Gemini and other non-OpenAI providers
source_issues.evidence: OpenAIConfig.store defaults to False. hasattr(self.config, 'store') is always True, so 'store': False is injected into every LLM call. Gemini rejects unknown 'store' field. Confirmed broken: Google Gemini via OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Likely affects Groq, Mistral, and all local OpenAI-compatible proxies.

signals.topic: TypeScript JS OSS: updateMemory/deleteMemory called with undefined ID when LLM returns out-of-range action.id — silent memory data loss
signals.summary: When the LLM returns an action.id not in the tempUuidMapping (hallucinated, out-of-range, or unexpected format), realMemoryId becomes undefined. updateMemory(undefined) and deleteMemory(undefined) are called, silently dropping the memory operation. No error propagates to the caller — only a log entry.
aliases: LLM action.id unresolvable causes silent data loss
signals.review_reason: Silent data loss in the JS OSS memory update/delete path is a critical reliability issue. Users have no indication that their intended memory operations were silently dropped. This directly undermines the memory system's core value proposition. The bug is confirmed with a clear code path and a guard-insertion fix suggested.

source_issues.title: [Bug][JS OSS] updateMemory/deleteMemory called with undefined ID when LLM returns out-of-range action.id
source_issues.evidence: tempUuidMapping maps numeric string keys to real UUIDs. If LLM hallucinates or returns out-of-range id: realMemoryId = undefined. updateMemory(undefined) and deleteMemory(undefined) silently dropped. Error: Memory with ID undefined not found logged. The memory that should have been updated/deleted is unchanged without any caller notification — silent data loss.

signals.topic: Streaming tool execution fails with HTTP 400 after tool calls when using OpenRouter or OpenAI (tool role message without preceding tool_calls)
signals.summary: When streaming agent execution with tool calls, the framework sends a 'tool' role message that is not preceded by an assistant message with matching tool_calls in the same request. Providers (OpenRouter, OpenAI) return HTTP 400, causing streaming to abort and the entire agent task to fail. This blocks the main agent execution loop when tools are used in streaming mode.
signals.review_reason: This blocks the main agent execution flow when tools are used in streaming mode. The error is a provider-level 400 that is caused by the framework incorrectly ordering or constructing message sequences — a clear user-blocking defect affecting agentic tool use workflows.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: Streaming fails with OpenRouter 400: tool role without preceding tool_calls
source_issues.evidence: Full stack trace shows agent task fails with ChatClientException wrapping HTTP 400. Provider error: 'messages with role tool must be a response to a preceeding message with tool_calls'. Streaming aborts and task fails entirely.

signals.topic: Passing tools=[...] on FoundryAgent.run() causes HTTP 400 when agent already has tools defined on the server
signals.summary: When running a Foundry-hosted agent that already has function tools defined server-side, passing tools=[...] in the client-side run() call sends the tools parameter to the API, which Foundry rejects with 'Not allowed when agent is specified'. The workaround (removing tools) results in empty responses when the model issues function calls, as no local dispatch occurs.
aliases: tools parameter not allowed with agent reference
signals.review_reason: This blocks a primary use pattern (running Foundry agents with local tool dispatch) by causing a hard API rejection. The workaround actively degrades functionality — local tool execution is disabled, leaving the agent unable to respond to tool calls.

source_issues.title: Python: [BUG]: ChatClientException 400 invalid_payload when passing [tools] with an agent reference
source_issues.evidence: HTTP 400: 'Not allowed when agent is specified'. Tool schema is embedded server-side but framework re-sends tool declarations to the service, which rejects them. Workaround of removing tools breaks local dispatch, resulting in empty responses.

signals.topic: Dependency conflict: azure-ai-agentserver-agentframework 1.0.0b17 cannot be installed alongside agent-framework 1.0.0 due to agent-framework-core version constraints
signals.summary: pip install fails when both azure-ai-agentserver-agentframework 1.0.0b17 and agent-framework 1.0.0 are required together. The hosting adapter package requires agent-framework-core<=1.0.0rc3 while the main framework pins agent-framework-core==1.0.0. This makes the hosting adapter library (required for deploying agents as Foundry Hosted Agents) unusable.
aliases: pip install dependency conflict hosting adapter
signals.review_reason: This completely blocks the Azure Foundry Hosted Agent deployment workflow. The azure-ai-agentserver-agentframework package is required to host agents via the Hosting Adapter Library, and its installation is broken by a hard dependency conflict.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: 1.0.0 Incompatible with azure-ai-agentserver-agentframework==1.0.0b17
source_issues.evidence: pip resolve failure: azure-ai-agentserver-agentframework 1.0.0b17 depends on agent-framework-core<=1.0.0rc3 while agent-framework 1.0.0 requires agent-framework-core==1.0.0. No compatible distribution exists.

signals.topic: agent-framework-github-copilot package fails at import time with github-copilot-sdk 0.2.x due to missing copilot.types module
signals.summary: Importing agent_framework_github_copilot raises ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'copilot.types'. This is caused by the github-copilot-sdk 0.2.x release restructuring its modules, breaking the public API of the agent-framework GitHub Copilot integration package. Multiple samples and tests are affected.
aliases: github copilot sdk 0.2 module not found
signals.review_reason: The GitHub Copilot agent integration fails immediately at import time, making the entire package unusable with the current SDK version. This is a hard startup crash for affected users.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: GitHub Copilot package incompatible with github-copilot-sdk 0.2.x
source_issues.evidence: Import raises ModuleNotFoundError immediately on module load. Multiple breaking API changes in SDK 0.2.x beyond module restructure affect _agent.py, tests, and 7 samples under python/samples/02-agents/providers/github_copilot/.

signals.topic: AzureAISearchContextProvider in agentic mode always returns None for source_data on knowledge base references, blocking citation metadata access
signals.summary: When using AzureAISearchContextProvider in agentic mode, ref.source_data is always None even when source_data_fields are correctly configured on the knowledge source. The root cause is that _agentic_search() does not pass include_reference_source_data=True in the knowledge_source_params on the KnowledgeBaseRetrievalRequest. This prevents consumers from accessing document names, page numbers, and content excerpts from retrieval references.
aliases: source_data always None Azure AI Search
signals.review_reason: This breaks citation functionality for RAG workflows using Azure AI Search in agentic mode. Users cannot access document/page metadata needed for answer attribution, which is a key enterprise requirement.

source_issues.title: Python: AzureAISearchContextProvider agentic mode: source_data is always None on references — missing include_reference_source_data parameter
source_issues.evidence: source_data is always None for every reference returned by agentic retrieval. Root cause identified: KnowledgeBaseRetrievalRequest is built without knowledge_source_params. A verified fix exists by injecting SearchIndexKnowledgeSourceParams with include_reference_source_data=True.

signals.topic: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor executes LLM-generated code without sandboxing, enabling arbitrary code execution and credential theft
signals.summary: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor writes LLM-generated code to disk and executes it as a subprocess with no sandboxing, filesystem isolation, or network restrictions. Only a UserWarning is emitted at init time, which is easily suppressed in production. Attackers can exploit indirect prompt injection to trigger execution of malicious code with full host privileges, leading to credential theft (SSH keys, cloud credentials, API tokens) and lateral movement.
aliases: LLM-generated code execution without security controls
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed security vulnerability with a concrete, realistic attack path. Users deploying LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor (following quickstart examples or for simplicity) who process untrusted input (user messages, web content, documents) are exposed to arbitrary code execution with full host privileges. The only safeguard is a UserWarning that is easily suppressed in production — not a real security control. This constitutes a primary flow failure (agents silently compromise the host) with significant cost/cost-impact (credential theft, lateral movement). Confirmed by automated security scanner (agent-audit) and mapped to OWASP ASI-09 and CWE-94.

source_issues.title: [Security] LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor executes LLM-generated code without sandboxing
source_issues.evidence: The executor writes LLM-generated code to a temp file and executes it via asyncio.create_subprocess_exec with no sandboxing. A UserWarning at construction time is the only safeguard, which is silently swallowed in most production configurations (e.g., -W ignore, logging pipelines). Attack scenario documented: indirect prompt injection tricks LLM into generating code that reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa and exfiltrates it. Impact: full system compromise, credential theft, lateral movement, data destruction.

signals.topic: Browser installation fails (CDN download errors / VSCode command generation bugs)
signals.summary: 用户运行 playwright install 时，浏览器下载因 CDN 返回 400 错误而失败；VSCode 扩展生成的 npm 命令语法错误（--browser=xxx 而非 --browser xxx），导致无法完成安装。两类问题共同导致用户无法正常安装浏览器，是主流程阻断。
signals.review_reason: 两类问题均直接阻断 Playwright 初始化主流程：CDN 错误使用户无法下载浏览器，VSCode 命令语法错误使扩展内置安装功能失效。count=2 有具体 issue 支撑，任意一种都会导致用户无法开始使用 Playwright。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Browser Download Fails with 400 GatewayExceptionResponse
source_issues.evidence: npx playwright install 失败，Azure CDN playwright.azureedge.net 返回 400 GatewayExceptionResponse，重试 5 次均失败，Chrome for Testing 147.0.7727.15 下载中止。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Test: Playwright Install in VSCode command Generated wrong command
source_issues.evidence: VSCode 命令面板 'Test: Playwright Install' 生成的命令使用 --browser=chromium --browser=firefox (=语法) 而非 --browser chromium firefox (空格语法)，导致 'too many arguments' 错误，浏览器安装无法完成。

signals.topic: Aria snapshot generation produces invalid snapshots causing test failures
signals.summary: 运行 npx playwright test --update-snapshots 时，aria snapshot 生成结果不是 deep equal，导致空或错误的 snapshot 文件无法被应用，测试全部失败。
signals.review_reason: 直接阻断测试运行主流程：--update-snapshots 生成的快照文件无法被应用，导致所有依赖该快照的测试失败。严重性高：用户信任 snapshot 作为 source of truth 的核心功能被破坏，且需要手动干预。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Generated Aria snapshots can fail in some circumstances because they are not deep equal
source_issues.evidence: npx playwright test --update-snapshots 生成的快照内容在特定 HTML 结构下不是 deep equal，导致生成的快照文件无法被应用，测试失败并需要手动修复。

signals.topic: MCP tool inputSchema includes $schema field causing all Anthropic API calls to fail with 400 error
signals.summary: MCP 服务器的 toMcpTool 函数在 inputSchema 中包含顶级 $schema 字段（来自 Zod v4 的 toJSONSchema），违反 MCP 协议规范，导致 Anthropic API 拒绝所有工具调用，返回 'JSON schema is invalid' 400 错误，且一个工具 schema 错误会导致整个会话所有工具调用全部失败。
signals.review_reason: MCP 是 Playwright 的关键 AI 集成功能。$schema 字段导致所有 Anthropic API 工具调用失败，且存在级联效应：一个工具的 schema 错误会使整个会话所有工具调用全部失效。这是关键功能不可用级别的问题。

source_issues.title: MCP: tool inputSchema includes $schema field, causing Anthropic API 400 errors
source_issues.evidence: MCP 服务器返回的 tool inputSchema 包含 $schema 顶级字段，MCP 协议禁止此字段，导致 Anthropic API 对所有工具调用返回 'JSON schema is invalid' 400 错误。一个 schema 错误导致整个会话内所有工具调用全部失败。

signals.topic: MCP server stale backend after disconnect — backendPromise not cleared in onClose
signals.summary: MCP server.ts 第 80 行 onClose 处理器在 dispose backend 时未清理 backendPromise，导致后续工具调用仍然 await 已 dispose 的 backend，返回 'Not connected' 错误，用户必须重启 MCP server 才能恢复。
signals.review_reason: MCP 连接断开后 server 进入不可用状态且无 work-around，必须重启进程才能恢复。严重影响依赖 MCP 进行 AI 自动化测试的用户体验，是关键功能可靠性问题。

source_issues.title: [MCP] backendPromise not cleared in onClose causes stale backend after disconnect
source_issues.evidence: onClose 处理器 dispose 了 backend 但未清理 backendPromise，后续工具调用 await 已 dispose 的 backend 并返回 'Not connected' 错误，仅重启 MCP server 可恢复，无用户端 work-around。

signals.topic: getByLabel fails to respect locator scope when duplicate label text exists
signals.summary: 当存在两个相同文本的 label 时（如两个 'Password'），locator.getByLabel('Password') 会找到 locator 作用域外的第一个 label 而非作用域内的那个，导致 fill 操作作用在错误元素上，引发测试不稳定或安全风险。
signals.review_reason: getByLabel 是 Playwright 核心 accessibility-based 定位 API，其 locator 作用域语义被破坏导致测试不稳定。更严重的是，在存在重复 label 的表单中可能向错误元素写入数据（安全隐患），是核心功能的正确性 bug。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: getByLabel failed in locator
source_issues.evidence: page.getByLabel('Username').fill('john') 后 page.locator('.box').getByLabel('Password').fill('secret') 因 getByLabel 找到作用域外第一个 'Password' 而超时；若两个相同 label 存在，locator 语义被违反，fill 可能作用在错误元素上（安全隐患）。

signals.topic: Google AI Gemini connector does not send tools/functions in API request — function calling completely broken
signals.summary: GoogleAIGeminiChatCompletion service omits the 'tools' field in outgoing API requests to Gemini, causing function calling to fail silently. Users see zero function calls returned despite correctly registering plugins.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断性 bug：function calling 是 Semantic Kernel 的核心功能，用户正确配置后完全不工作（functionCalls 始终为 0），且有明确 HTTP 请求日志证据证明 'tools' 字段被遗漏。issue 活跃超过 4 个月，8 条评论，说明持续影响用户。

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: GoogleAIGeminiChatCompletion doesn't send tools/functions in API request
source_issues.evidence: FunctionChoiceBehavior configured correctly but 'tools' field absent from API request payload; functionCalls.Count is always 0 despite registered plugins; user confirmed same config works via OpenAI-compatible Gemini endpoint, ruling out plugin/settings misconfiguration

signals.topic: Google AI connector leaks model thinking/reasoning text into application-visible ChatMessageContent
signals.summary: When Gemini thinking/thought parts are enabled, internal reasoning text leaks into the response content returned to the application, polluting actual model answers with intermediate reasoning steps.
signals.review_reason: 体验降级：模型内部推理内容混入应用可见响应，导致下游用户看到混乱/错误的输出。在 function calling 流程中尤其严重，最终响应被中间推理步骤污染。issue 有明确复现步骤和泄漏示例内容。

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: Google AI connector leaks thinking/thought text parts into ChatMessageContent
source_issues.evidence: With gemini-3-pro-preview and thinking_config enabled, model internal reasoning (e.g. '**Processing the Task Request** Okay, the task creation was successful...') appears in final ChatMessageContent instead of the actual answer; affects auto function calling pipeline; fix identified as adding part.thought filtering

signals.topic: ExtensionData custom parameters silently dropped from HTTP request — user-configured options not sent to API
signals.summary: Custom parameters added via ExtensionData in OpenAIPromptExecutionSettings (e.g. enable_thinking) are silently ignored and not included in the HTTP JSON payload, preventing users from passing provider-specific options.
aliases: custom parameters not in request payload
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：用户明确配置了参数但系统静默忽略，导致无法控制模型行为（如 enable_thinking）。静默失败比显式报错危害更大，用户无法诊断问题根因。

source_issues.title: Bug: ExtensionData parameters not included in HTTP JSON request when using OpenAIPromptExecutionSettings
source_issues.evidence: User sets ExtensionData with enable_thinking: false but field is absent from generated JSON; 9 comments indicating active user interest; affects all providers using OpenAIPromptExecutionSettings

signals.topic: AgentGroupChat message duplication when attempting to pass full chat history to agents
signals.summary: When users try to pass complete conversation history to individual agents within AgentGroupChat, messages duplicate and multiply with each agent turn, with no clean thread-equivalent API available.
aliases: Chat history duplication in group chat
signals.review_reason: 多 agent 场景核心阻断：无法向 AgentGroupChat 中的 agent 传递完整对话历史，多 agent 编排的基础能力缺失。用户尝试自行 hack 但引入指数级消息重复，11 条评论说明社区广泛关注。

source_issues.title: .Net: Python: Cannot pass the full chat history to a specific agent in AgentGroupChat without message duplication
source_issues.evidence: User attempted to modify ChatHistoryChannel.invoke to pass full history but triggered exponential message duplication as agents bounce between turns; no thread API equivalent like single-agent get_response; 11 comments active community issue; blocks multi-agent orchestration

signals.topic: Amazon Bedrock image-to-text (captioning) completely broken across multiple image formats
signals.summary: BedrockChatCompletionService fails to process image content for captioning across all tested MIME types (png, jpeg, bmp), causing models to respond that no image was provided.
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：图片captioning功能在Bedrock连接器上完全失效，用户被迫切换到Azure OpenAI才能工作。同一份代码对比证明了问题在SK连接器侧（ImageContent元数据序列化），且覆盖所有常见图片格式。

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Amazon BedrockChatCompletionService image-to-text (captioning) not working
source_issues.evidence: Same C# code fails on Bedrock (Claude 3.5 Sonnet) but works on Azure OpenAI (GPT-4o); tested all three MIME types (png/jpeg/bmp); raw requests.post with Bedrock Converse API works, proving image data is correct; bug is in SK's connector serialization of ImageContent metadata

signals.topic: MCP server startup/handshake fails for local stdio servers
signals.summary: Codex CLI fails to complete MCP handshake for local stdio servers on Linux, with Codex never sending messages or incorrectly handling the initialize response, despite the server working correctly when tested standalone.
signals.review_reason: Blocks MCP tool integration — a core Codex extensibility feature. Users cannot connect local stdio MCP servers reliably; CLI misreports healthy MCP servers as having no tools. MCP is a differentiating feature and its failure to start is a direct workflow block. Two independent reports on the same day confirm this is a consistent, reproducible regression.

source_issues.title: Codex CLI MCP startup fails for local stdio server even though manual initialize succeeds
source_issues.evidence: MCP client for test-server timed out after 60 seconds. Server starts and completes initialization, but Codex never sends any MCP message. Also manifests as 'handshaking with MCP server failed: connection closed: initialize response'. Validated with manual stdio testing that server returns correct initialize response.

source_issues.title: Codex CLI /mcp can show 'Tools: (none)' while MCP tools are callable
source_issues.evidence: CLI /mcp command reports 'No MCP tools available' and 'Tools: (none)' even when MCP tools are callable in the same session. Misleads users into thinking MCP is broken while runtime tool calls still succeed. Status rendering bug in CLI MCP discovery.

signals.topic: Windows sandbox cannot detect per-user PATH programs and fails due to PowerShell profile
signals.summary: On Windows, the sandboxed terminal fails to find per-user installed programs (npm via fnm in AppData/Roaming) and also loads the user's PowerShell profile which causes command failures due to unavailable profile dependencies.
signals.review_reason: Two related Windows sandbox failures: (1) per-user PATH programs not visible inside sandbox — blocks npm, node, and similar tools that developers rely on daily; (2) user PowerShell profile loaded inside sandbox causes cascading command failures with misleading errors. Both directly break development workflows on the Windows platform, which is a primary Codex target.

source_issues.title: Codex Terminal in Windows Sandbox doesn't detect programs
source_issues.evidence: npm command works in host terminal but 'npm --version' inside sandboxed Codex terminal returns 'The term npm is not recognized'. Root cause: per-user npm installed at AppData/Roaming/fnm/ is not in sandbox PATH.

source_issues.title: Sandbox limits powershell behavior
source_issues.evidence: Sandbox loads user's default PowerShell profile which runs fnm env setup and Import-Module for WinGet CommandNotFound. Both fail inside sandbox, causing Get-ChildItem and other commands to produce misleading errors instead of clean output.

signals.topic: Quota tracking incorrect — users blocked despite available budget
signals.summary: Users with active API quota (e.g., $120 balance, weekly quota remaining) are shown 'Quota exceeded' or 'Model at capacity' errors, indicating a quota accounting or admission-control bug.
signals.review_reason: Direct cost-loss and workflow block: users with paid API subscriptions and verified available quota are denied service. Both incidents show paid users blocked from using the product they are paying for. Without clear error messaging, users cannot self-diagnose whether this is a billing bug, a capacity management issue, or an account entitlement routing error. Destroys trust in the billing system.

source_issues.title: Quota exceeded. Check your plan and billing details.
source_issues.evidence: User provided API key, used less than $1 out of $120 budget. Logged out and logged back in, provided key again — error persists. gpt-5.4 on API plan.

source_issues.title: Codex CLI recommends gpt-5.4, then fails with 'Selected model is at capacity' despite available quota
source_issues.evidence: User had 5-hour and weekly Codex quota largely available. Codex promoted gpt-5.4 migration, then turn failed with 'Selected model is at capacity'. Later requests on same model succeeded — transient but real admission/capacity failure with no clear explanation.

signals.topic: Auth token refresh does not propagate to existing live sessions
signals.summary: When an API-based authentication token expires and is refreshed externally, existing live Codex CLI sessions remain stuck at 401 Unauthorized and cannot recover without manual restart.
aliases: auth refresh not detected by live sessions
signals.review_reason: Auth refresh failure in headless/Corporate use case blocks active sessions and forces manual restart. Corporate users with long-running headless sessions are particularly impacted — their sessions cannot self-heal after a token refresh. This is a session state management bug that causes repeated manual intervention for automation workflows.

source_issues.title: Live codex cli session cannot continue on auth refresh (api login)
source_issues.evidence: Corporate user with API-based auth. Token expires (auth.json mutated). External refresh via separate CLI does not fix the pre-existing live session. Session enters reconnect loop: 1/5 → 2/5 → 3/5 → 4/5 → 5/5 → 401 NotAuthenticated. 'High impact on headless Codex use.'

signals.topic: File paths with non-ASCII characters (Chinese/space) fail to open in VS Code
signals.summary: Codex app cannot open files with Chinese characters or spaces in the path when clicking file citations, causing wrong files to open or failures.
aliases: spaces in file path not handled
signals.review_reason: Breaks the core file citation UX — a fundamental Codex feature. Files with non-ASCII characters in paths (common in Chinese, Japanese, Korean, and other localized environments) cannot be opened correctly. This is not an edge case in international markets where non-ASCII directory and file names are the norm.

source_issues.title: codex app can not open file in vscode when the path has chinese or space
source_issues.evidence: Clicking a file path with spaces or Chinese characters opens the wrong file (or a blank file). Reported with screenshot evidence showing incorrect file opening behavior.

signals.topic: GPT-5.1/GPT-5.4 /responses endpoint silently hangs 10–28% of concurrent requests with no error response
signals.summary: Under moderate concurrent load (5 simultaneous calls), the /v1/responses endpoint silently drops 10–28% of requests: no HTTP error, no timeout, no SDK retry. TCP handshake completes but no response ever arrives. The SDK's wait_for loop hangs indefinitely until caller-kill.
signals.review_reason: High-frequency silent failure (10–28%) in a core workflow path (concurrent agent calls). No error, no timeout, no retry — completely invisible to the SDK. Affects the primary agent execution path in production. Count=1 but reviewer_reason provides strong evidence: reproducible across multiple test runs with table-formatted data, affecting concurrent production workloads. Raw client confirmation rules out SDK bug.

source_issues.title: GPT-5.1 / GPT-5.4 /responses endpoint silently hangs 10-28% of concurrent requests
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible 10–28% hung rate across 4 test runs with 50 calls each. Both raw AsyncOpenAI and Agents SDK hang at the same rate, confirming server-side issue. Hung requests produce no error, no timeout — caller must kill. Production impact: agents silently stall with no fallback.

signals.topic: Traces silently dropped in long-running workers (Celery, FastAPI background tasks, RQ, Dramatiq)
signals.summary: BatchTraceProcessor only auto-flushes on process shutdown. Long-running workers never shut down, so traces remain buffered forever and never appear on the platform traces dashboard. No error or warning is emitted.
aliases: trace buffer never flushed in background workers
missing trace flush in worker processes
signals.review_reason: Silently blocks observability in a common production pattern (long-running workers). Traces appear to work (valid IDs logged) but are actually lost, making debugging impossible. The pattern affects Celery, FastAPI background tasks, RQ, and Dramatiq — all widely used. No error is raised, so users have no indication traces are missing.

source_issues.title: Traces are silently dropped in long-running workers
source_issues.evidence: Traces created correctly (valid IDs, nesting works) but never appear on platform dashboard in Celery/FastAPI background tasks. BatchTraceProcessor only flushes on shutdown. No error/warning emitted. 3-line workaround confirmed effective.

signals.topic: SDK crashes with TypeError when upstream provider returns error payload with null choices
signals.summary: When a provider returns an error JSON payload, the SDK returns a ChatCompletion-shaped object where choices is None. The SDK's debug logger immediately dereferences response.choices[0], raising TypeError inside the SDK before the application can handle the error.
aliases: TypeError in openai_chatcompletions.py on provider error
signals.review_reason: SDK crashes (TypeError) in a legitimate error path — when a provider returns an error payload. Users cannot gracefully handle provider errors because the crash occurs inside the SDK before exception propagation. This blocks error recovery and forces application-level workarounds.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: SDK crashes when `choices` is `None` (provider-error payload)
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible with mockup: passing sk-dummy key to OpenAIChatCompletionsModel causes TypeError 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable inside SDK before application can catch the error. Affects any provider (OpenRouter, proxies, etc.) that returns error-shaped responses.

signals.topic: RedisSession blocks async event loop causing streaming events to never emit in production (run_streamed)
signals.summary: When using agents.extensions.memory.RedisSession with RedisSession, run_streamed() hangs indefinitely. Logs show 'run_streamed returned, consuming stream_events' but 'First run_item_stream_event received' never fires. The session's first Redis call blocks the event loop before it can produce events.
aliases: run_streamed hangs in production with Redis
signals.review_reason: Production-blocking bug: run_streamed() completely fails to emit events when RedisSession is used. Core streaming functionality is non-functional. The user investigated thoroughly (confirmed event loop blocking as root cause, confirmed session=None works), indicating a real and significant production problem.

source_issues.title: Using redis to preserve chat sessions in prod
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed: with session=None, streaming works; with RedisSession, producer run_loop_task never emits events. Logs show 'run_streamed returned, consuming stream_events' but no events follow. RedisSession's first call blocks event loop in async context.

signals.topic: Agent loops trigger runaway API calls causing significant cost loss in production
signals.summary: An agent loop triggered thousands of unexpected API calls, causing cost overrun. The author explicitly states they ran into this situation and is asking how others handle cost limits, fallback behavior, and oncall responsibility before deploying agents.
signals.review_reason: User explicitly reports runaway agent loop causing thousands of API calls — a concrete cost loss incident. While framed as a question, the author self-reports a production incident. Lack of built-in cost limits/fallbacks is a systemic gap affecting production deployments.

source_issues.title: How are you handling cost / safety checks before deploying agents?
source_issues.evidence: Author explicitly states: 'We ran into a situation where an agent loop triggered thousands of API calls unexpectedly.' This is a direct account of cost loss from uncontrolled agent behavior. Multiple community responses indicate this is a shared concern.

signals.topic: Responses API endpoint silently hangs 10-28% of concurrent requests with no error or retry
signals.summary: Under moderate concurrent load (5 simultaneous calls), the /v1/responses endpoint silently drops 10-28% of requests. Affected requests receive no HTTP error, no timeout response, and no SDK retry — the TCP connection hangs indefinitely until the caller's timeout kills it. Reproduced with both raw AsyncOpenAI client and Agents SDK, confirming the root cause is server-side (confirmed via cf-ray headers hitting Cloudflare/SJC).
signals.review_reason: Severe user-facing workflow disruption: 10-28% of requests fail silently with zero visibility — no error, no timeout signal, no SDK retry. Users have no way to detect or recover from these failures programmatically. The reporter provided detailed reproducible test data across multiple models (gpt-5.1, gpt-5.4) and runs. Although the reporter attributes the root cause to the server-side /v1/responses endpoint (not the SDK), this is a primary pain point for Python SDK users as the issue is filed in the SDK repo and affects real production usage. P0 despite count=1 because review_reason provides overwhelming user impact evidence: high failure rate (up to 28%), complete absence of error/timeout signaling, confirmed across multiple models and hours of testing, and no SDK-side recovery mechanism.

source_issues.title: GPT-5.1 / GPT-5.4 /responses endpoint silently hangs 10-28% of concurrent requests
source_issues.evidence: Reporter ran 50 concurrent calls across 4 test runs and measured 8%, 10%, 16%, and 28% hang rates. Both raw AsyncOpenAI and Agents SDK hang at the same rate, confirming server-side root cause. Hung requests receive no HTTP response, no error, and no SDK retry. TCP handshake completes but no response body is ever sent. Successful requests from the same batch return in <1s, ruling out network-level issues.

signals.topic: Responses API null text field causes SDK crash in response parsing
signals.summary: When the OpenAI API returns an output_text content item with a null text field, the Python SDK's Response.output_text property and responses.parse() both fail. The strict model validation rejects ResponseOutputText.text = null, and structured parsing throws errors on null output_text items. This blocks all usage of the Responses API for any payload containing null text entries.
signals.review_reason: Critical workflow-blocking bug in the Python SDK: when the API returns output_text items with null text fields (a valid API response), the SDK raises validation errors and crashes. This makes the Responses API unusable for any payload hitting this edge case. The bug is confirmed in SDK model validation (pydantic strict mode rejects null text), and the reporter provides a complete reproducible example. The issue is labeled 'bug' and a related PR #3062 confirms the team is working on a fix. Despite count=1, P0 because the user impact is severe and unambiguous: a specific SDK feature (Responses API parsing) becomes completely unusable, the failure is in the user's critical path (parsing API responses), and the fix is within SDK control. This is a main-flow failure for Responses API consumers.

source_issues.title: Response.output_text and responses.parse fail when an output_text item has text: null
source_issues.evidence: Reporter provides a complete reproducible payload with a null text output_text item alongside a valid one. The SDK raises a validation error on Response.model_validate(data). The issue is confirmed as a bug in the SDK's pydantic model validation — the ResponseOutputText model does not accept null for the text field even though the API can return it. Related PR #3062 exists, indicating the team is aware of the issue.

signals.topic: Persistent sessions die immediately after creation — queue owner unavailable on macOS
signals.summary: On macOS, newly-created persistent sessions immediately report status=dead with 'queue owner unavailable'. The queue owner process either exits immediately or is incorrectly marked as dead by the health probe. Thread-bound ACP sessions are completely unstable; users must disable threading as a workaround.
signals.review_reason: Issue #185: macOS上持久会话创建后立即 report status=dead，queue owner 不可用，用户被阻断在 thread-bound session（OpenClaw thread 功能依赖此机制）。Issue #29: Claude 13/13 会话均以 0 turns + connection_close 结束，每次会话都立即失败。两 issues 根因相同（queue owner 与 session 生命周期问题），共同证明持久会话在 macOS 上完全不可用，是主流程阻断。

source_issues.title: Persistent sessions become dead immediately (queue owner unavailable) on macOS
source_issues.evidence: sessions ensure succeeds but status immediately returns dead with summary=queue owner unavailable. Confirmed queue owner process exists (ps aux shows pid). Downstream OpenClaw logs show 'acpx ensureSession replacing dead named session'. Root cause: either queue owner exits immediately or health probe incorrectly marks it dead. Workaround: mode=run, thread=false (disable threading). macmini16 user blocked from using thread-bound sessions.

source_issues.title: Claude ACP agent fails: all sessions end with 0 turns, agent disconnects after ~3s
source_issues.evidence: 13/13 Claude sessions failed with 0 turns each. Session record shows lastAgentDisconnectReason=connection_close, agent exits ~2.6s after start. Queue owner stays alive but Claude agent subprocess dies. Identical config works for Codex (3/3 completed). Clear user impact: every persistent Claude session immediately fails.

signals.topic: `sessions new` hangs indefinitely with zero output, blocking session-based workflow
signals.summary: Both `acpx opencode sessions new` and `acpx claude sessions new` hang indefinitely (zero output, exit 124) on all platforms, while `acpx exec` works correctly. The session creation command is completely non-functional, forcing users to fall back to one-shot exec mode only.
signals.review_reason: sessions new 命令在所有平台上挂起（零输出，超时退出 124），完全阻断了持久会话这一核心功能流程。用户被迫降级为仅能用 exec 单次模式，无法使用多轮对话。issue 提供了完整的复现步骤、退出码和多版本对比证据，属于主流程阻断级别。

source_issues.title: [Bug] sessions new hangs with zero output while exec works fine — affects both opencode and claude
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction shows acpx opencode/claude exec works; acpx opencode/claude sessions new hangs with zero output and times out at 20s (exit 124). Issue filed by OpenClaw agent on behalf of the user, affecting both agents identically across versions 0.4.0 and 0.4.1. This is a complete functional block on the persistent session workflow.

signals.topic: CLI `--session` flag silently ignored in exec mode — AI agents waste API credits on wrong execution context
signals.summary: The top-level `acpx claude --session xxx prompt` command looks like it should use a named session but actually runs in exec (one-shot) mode, silently ignoring `--session`. An AI agent reported writing the wrong command 3 times in a row, wasting user time and API credits each time. The fix should either throw an error or route to session mode.
signals.review_reason: CLI 顶层 --session 参数被静默忽略，导致 AI agent 在 3 次连续尝试中都用了错误命令，每次都浪费用户时间和 API 费用。不同于普通功能请求，这是一个导致真实资源损耗的 UX 设计缺陷。用户明确指出每次错误都有实际成本损失。

source_issues.title: CLI command structure is extremely confusing for AI agents — acpx claude vs acpx claude prompt vs acpx claude exec
source_issues.evidence: AI agent (J.A.R.V.I.S.) wrote wrong command 3 times consecutively: each attempt used acpx claude --session which silently ran exec mode (not session mode). Each mistake wastes user time and API credits. The --session flag on top-level command is silently ignored with no warning or error. The acpx exec command doesn't even support --session but also silently ignores it.

signals.topic: `--no-wait` submits prompts to queue but queue owner never processes them — fire-and-forget prompts silently lost
signals.summary: Using `--no-wait` to submit fire-and-forget prompts queues the job but the queue owner never processes it. The command returns [queued] immediately but the prompt is never executed. Workaround is to use `--timeout` instead, which blocks but correctly processes the prompt. This causes silent data loss in automation scripts.
signals.review_reason: --no-wait 提交 fire-and-forget 任务时，任务进入队列但 queue owner 永不处理，导致静默丢失用户任务。自动化脚本依赖此行为时会丢失工作而没有任何错误提示。Queue owner 进程存活但无法取走任务，问题定位清晰（有明确复现步骤和 workaround 证据），属于关键功能非阻断性失败。

source_issues.title: [BUG] --no-wait queues prompt but queue owner never processes it
source_issues.evidence: acpx --approve-all codex --no-wait 'Create /tmp/test.txt' queues job immediately ([queued] <job-id>) but file is never created. Queue owner process is alive (ps aux confirms pid) but never picks up the queued job. Session status shows 'running' with pid but no work done. Regular prompts without --no-wait work fine. Workaround: use --timeout instead (blocks but processes correctly). Silent data loss in automation.

signals.topic: No reasoning effort configuration support for Claude agent — feature request vs. feature gap affecting production review runs
signals.summary: acpx translates `thought_level` to `reasoning_effort` for Codex but passes it through unchanged for Claude. Claude's ACP agent ignores `thought_level` entirely, and acpx doesn't read `MODEL_REASONING_EFFORT` env var. Production review pipelines (codiscover-ai/agent) specify `reasoning_effort: max` which is silently ignored for Claude runs.
signals.review_reason: Claude 推理努力配置在 acpx 中完全缺失，导致生产环境 codiscover-ai/agent 的 Claude review runs 指定 max 推理级别被静默忽略。但此 issue 核心是功能缺失而非用户流程失败，优先级 P2。

source_issues.title: Support reasoning effort configuration for Claude agent
source_issues.evidence: acpx codex set thought_level xhigh → correctly translated to reasoning_effort. acpx claude set thought_level max → no-op (Claude ACP agent ignores it). Production codiscover-ai/agent review runs specify reasoning_effort: max but it's silently ignored for Claude. flow run has no flag/env-var/sessionOptions field for reasoning effort at all.

signals.topic: Security scanner generates widespread false positive suspicious flags on legitimate skills

Root patterns flagged incorrectly include: fs file I/O (legitimate), local git commands, read-only public API calls, webhook calls to author's own endpoints, x402 client-side wallet auth examples, and metadata extraction bugs. Volume and diversity of false positives indicate systematic scanner accuracy issues damaging marketplace trust.
