signals.topic: ClawHub website completely broken in Safari — SyntaxError blocks all pages
signals.summary: ClawHub website (clawhub.ai) throws a SyntaxError in Safari/WebKit JavaScriptCore, causing complete website unavailability. Affects all users on Safari browsers (macOS).
signals.review_reason: Website completely blocked for Safari users (all pages). Confirmed on multiple installations. This is a P0 browser compatibility issue that prevents any user interaction.

source_issues.title: Safari (WebKit/JavaScriptCore) SyntaxError: Unexpected keyword 'in' on website pages
source_issues.evidence: Website functionality is completely blocked in Safari; confirmed on multiple macOS Safari installations across homepage and skill pages.

signals.topic: GitHub OAuth login succeeds but no session cookie is created — users cannot log in
signals.summary: GitHub OAuth authorization completes (302 redirect) but no session cookie is set, leaving users permanently logged out. Likely caused by stale/soft-deleted user record conflict.
signals.review_reason: Authentication flow is fundamentally broken — OAuth succeeds but login fails silently, completely preventing user access to their account. This is a core auth bug despite low count.

source_issues.title: GitHub OAuth callback succeeds (302) but no session is created
source_issues.evidence: OAuth code exchange completes successfully but session creation fails silently with no error surfaced to user. User remains logged out after OAuth redirect.

signals.topic: clawhub explore --json always returns empty items[] in all sort modes
signals.summary: The `clawhub explore` command returns `{"items": [], "nextCursor": null}` for all sort modes (newest, downloads, rating, installs, trending), blocking dashboard builds and skill discovery tools.
signals.review_reason: Core CLI command is functionally broken across all modes, blocking legitimate use cases (dashboard with download/star stats). The web UI shows data exists but the CLI returns nothing.

source_issues.title: clawhub explore --json returns empty items[] (authenticated, all sort modes)
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced with valid auth token across all sort modes; web interface shows 48K+ skills but CLI returns nothing. Blocks dashboard building use case requiring download/star statistics.

signals.topic: Skill organization transfer fails with 'User not found' — prevents team publishing workflows
signals.summary: Users cannot transfer personal skills to organization accounts using `clawhub transfer`, receiving 'User not found' error. Blocks organization publishing and team collaboration.
signals.review_reason: Key team workflow (transferring skills to organization for collaborative publishing) is completely blocked. Users cannot share skills with their organization.

source_issues.title: How can I transfer "personal skills" to "organization skills"
source_issues.evidence: User has created an organization and wants to transfer skills so others can publish, but `bun clawhub transfer` returns 'User not found'. Entire organization publishing workflow is blocked.

signals.topic: Parser corrupts --args-json payloads with escaped characters, breaking workflow execution
signals.summary: The tokenizer/parser incorrectly handles escaped characters inside quoted arguments, corrupting JSON passed through --args-json before it reaches command handlers. Escaped apostrophes in single-quoted args cause parse failures (Unclosed quote), and backslashes in double-quoted JSON alter escape sequences, changing payload semantics. This breaks pipelines that pass prompt-rich JSON with special characters.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed bug with concrete reproduction steps. Parser corruption of --args-json payloads is a main-flow breakage for workflows passing JSON with special characters. Issue #17 was closed with a fix, confirming it was a real bug, not a feature request.

source_issues.title: Parser mishandles escaped characters in quoted args, breaking --args-json payloads
source_issues.evidence: Two concrete failure modes documented with shell reproduction commands. Backslash-in-double-quoted args corrupts JSON escape sequences, altering payload semantics. Escaped apostrophe in single-quoted JSON causes 'Unclosed quote' parse failure. Both break pipelines that pass prompt-rich JSON through --args-json.

signals.topic: Approval tokens too long for Telegram/Discord inline buttons, blocking human-in-the-loop on top chat platforms
signals.summary: Lobster approval gates generate base64-encoded JWT-style resume tokens (~150+ chars). Telegram's inline button payload limit is 64 bytes and Discord's is 100 chars, both too small. This means the core human-in-the-loop approval mechanism cannot be presented as one-tap buttons on the two most popular chat surfaces. Users must copy-paste long tokens instead of tapping a button.
signals.review_reason: Core human-in-the-loop feature is broken on the two most popular chat platforms (Telegram, Discord) due to token length exceeding platform button payload limits. This is a significant UX degradation where the intended one-tap approval flow is completely unavailable, forcing users into copy-paste workflows. The issue was closed after implementation, confirming it was a genuine user pain point.

source_issues.title: Approval tokens too long for chat-surface buttons (Telegram, Discord)
source_issues.evidence: Issue provides a platform comparison table showing Telegram (64 bytes) and Discord (100 chars) cannot fit ~150+ char approval tokens. Approval gates — the core human-in-the-loop mechanism — cannot be presented as one-tap buttons. Author documents a brittle two-step hack as current workaround. Closed with a fix, confirming the problem was real.

signals.topic: Windows: ollama launch openclaw creates duplicate gateway when Scheduled Task is already running
signals.summary: On Windows, running `ollama launch openclaw` while the gateway already runs as a Scheduled Task in Session 0 spawns a second node.exe process that also binds to port 18789, causing port conflicts, mDNS name collisions, EPERM file errors, and mass handshake timeouts.
aliases: Session 0 process isolation causes duplicate gateway
gateway port conflict on Windows Scheduled Task
signals.review_reason: 虽然count=1，但issue #151明确描述了主流程阻断：用户执行核心命令ollama launch openclaw时因Session 0进程隔离机制导致重复启动gateway，产生端口冲突、mDNS冲突、EPERM文件错误、RPC和握手超时等多种并发故障。症状链完整，用户影响证据充分，属于P1级别非预期并发进程类用户痛点。

source_issues.title: [Windows] ollama launch openclaw starts duplicate gateway when Scheduled Task is already running
source_issues.evidence: User reports two LISTENING entries on port 18789, mDNS name conflict 'DESKTOP-xxx (OpenClaw) (2)', RPC probe failures, EPERM errors on pending.json, and mass handshake timeout / gateway closed (1006) errors. Root cause: user-session process enumeration cannot see Session 0 processes.

signals.topic: Windows Tray App does not auto-reconnect after Gateway restart, leaving node disconnected indefinitely
signals.summary: After a Gateway restart, the Windows Tray App node remains permanently disconnected and never attempts reconnection, unlike the CLI node which retries automatically. Users must manually toggle Node Mode off and on to recover.
aliases: Tray App node disconnection after gateway restart
no automatic node reconnection in Tray App
signals.review_reason: Gateway重启后Tray App节点永久断开且无任何自动重连行为，CLI节点则正常重连——不一致的恢复机制导致用户体验断裂，用户必须手动操作才能恢复，属于关键功能的非预期不可用状态。症状日志完整，对比CLI行为证据清晰，keep=true。

source_issues.title: Windows Tray App does not auto-reconnect after Gateway restart
source_issues.evidence: User reports node stays permanently disconnected after gateway restart with no reconnection attempts logged. CLI node correctly logs 'Node reconnecting in 1000ms (attempt 1)'. Tray App requires manual toggle of Node Mode off/on as workaround.

signals.topic: Gateway memory leak causes silent OOM crashes every 1-2 hours, killing active agent runs
signals.summary: Gateway RSS grows from ~560MB to 3-4GB within 1-2 hours then crashes silently with no log entry. Active agent runs are killed with process_lost, forcing retries and wasting LLM tokens and time.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow is completely blocked as active agent runs are killed every 1-2 hours. This is a persistent, reproducible blocking issue with 6 gateway restarts in 12 hours confirmed. Tasks must be retried, wasting LLM tokens and compute time. The silent nature of the crash (no log entry) makes it particularly difficult to diagnose without explicit memory profiling.

source_issues.title: v2026.4.2 gateway memory leak: RSS grows to 3-4GB within 1-2 hours, silent OOM crash
source_issues.evidence: Gateway RSS grows from ~560MB to 3-4GB within 1-2 hours then crashes silently with no SIGTERM, no heap error, no log entry before crash. 6 restarts observed in 12 hours. Active agent runs killed with process_lost. Paperclip integration sees repeated failures for long-running tasks (>15 min runs impossible).

signals.topic: Telegram approval prompts delivered to wrong DM — cross-chat isolation failure
signals.summary: A host approval prompt initiated in Jeffe's Telegram DM surfaced in Sarah's separate Telegram DM. The wrong person can see command details and approve or deny them.
signals.review_reason: This crosses a security/trust boundary — approval prompts for host-level commands are delivered to the wrong user across separate Telegram DMs. The wrong person can see command details and approve or deny operational actions. This is not merely a UX issue but an authorization leak between users in the same Telegram deployment.

source_issues.title: OpenClaw 4.5 regression: Telegram approval prompts can surface in the wrong DM
source_issues.evidence: A host approval prompt initiated in Jeffe's Telegram DM surfaced in Sarah's separate Telegram DM. This is a cross-chat isolation failure where one allowlisted user receives operational approval prompts created by another user's session. The wrong person can see host diagnostic command details and potentially approve or deny them, crossing a trust boundary.

signals.topic: Telegram DM session hangs or becomes unresponsive after /new or /reset command (v2026.4.5 regression)
signals.summary: After /new or /reset in Telegram DMs, replies are delayed or appear hung with invalid session header. Gateway restart is required to recover.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow is blocked in Telegram DMs after using /new or /reset — a core user interaction. Users must restart the gateway to recover, which is an unacceptable workaround for a common command. This is a regression in 4.5 affecting the primary communication channel for DM users. The session-memory hook reading transient state is a reproducible race condition on every /new or /reset.

source_issues.title: OpenClaw 4.5 regression: session-memory can race /new and /reset rotation in Telegram DMs
source_issues.evidence: After /new or /reset in Telegram DMs with dmScope=per-channel-peer, replies are delayed or appear hung. Session enters timeout-compaction weirdness with 'invalid session header' despite gateway being otherwise healthy. Gateway restart snaps it back. Groups and WebUI do not show the same pattern — DM-specific. Bundled session-memory hook is suspected of reading half-written JSONL during reset rotation.

signals.topic: Signal messages cannot be received — SSE stream connection fails with TypeError terminated
signals.summary: OpenClaw cannot receive Signal messages. SSE stream connection fails with TypeError terminated. signal-cli daemon HTTP server starts fine and JSON-RPC works, but receiving does not.
signals.review_reason: Signal integration is completely broken — messages cannot be received at all while sending works fine. This is a total failure of one messaging channel, not a degradation. The SSE stream handler is terminating immediately, indicating a fundamental compatibility issue with signal-cli 0.14.x.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: OpenClaw cannot receive Signal messages
source_issues.evidence: OpenClaw cannot receive Signal messages. SSE stream connection fails with 'TypeError: terminated'. signal-cli daemon HTTP server starts fine and JSON-RPC works, but OpenClaw's SSE fetch gets terminated immediately. Sending messages works, receiving does not. Regression in 2026.4.5.

signals.topic: message send command crashes with ERR_INTERNAL_ASSERTION in v2026.4.5, blocking all push notifications
signals.summary: On v2026.4.5, message send exits immediately with ERR_INTERNAL_ASSERTION thrown from command-registry. The entire message subtree (send, broadcast, edit, delete, react, poll) is affected.
signals.review_reason: Critical regression blocking all message send operations across all channels in v2026.4.5. The entire message subtree is affected, blocking push notifications, broadcasts, and scheduled dispatches. Production deployments relying on any outbound messaging are completely broken. Workaround is to pin to v2026.4.2.

source_issues.title: `message send` crashes with `ERR_INTERNAL_ASSERTION` in v2026.4.5 (regression from v2026.4.2)
source_issues.evidence: On v2026.4.5, message send exits immediately with ERR_INTERNAL_ASSERTION thrown from command-registry at module-registration time before any send attempt. Same command on v2026.4.2 succeeds and returns Message ID. The entire message subtree (send, broadcast, edit, delete, react, poll) is affected. Blocks push notifications, broadcast messaging, agent-to-channel relays, and scheduled message dispatches.

signals.topic: Non-string `.lower()` crash on multimodal image requests
signals.summary: When users send multimodal requests containing images, a `.lower()` call on a non-string object causes a crash, breaking the main execution flow.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed code-level bug (PR #1477) that crashes the main execution flow when users send multimodal (image) requests. While the count is 1 (single source), the bug is confirmed on main and represents a clear user-blocking condition: any user attempting to use vision/image capabilities will encounter an unhandled exception, making it P1 rather than P2.

source_issues.title: Qodo AntiSlop scan found 46 issues across 10 recent PRs
source_issues.evidence: Automated scan confirmed this bug still exists on main branch (PR #1477). The `.lower()` call in the multimodal handler receives a non-string object (likely image bytes/URL) instead of text, causing an unhandled TypeError that crashes the request.

signals.topic: Missing API key prompt for provider-prefixed model names
signals.summary: Users with provider-prefixed model names (e.g., 'provider/model-name') do not receive a prompt to enter their API key, causing silent failures or unclear errors when the key is missing.
aliases: provider-prefixed model API key not requested
missing API key prompt for third-party models
signals.review_reason: Confirmed bug (PR #1418) on main branch where provider-prefixed model names bypass the API key prompt, causing users to hit silent/cryptic auth failures. The impact is clear (key auth path broken), but count=1 and no direct user reports in the dataset, so P2 is appropriate.

source_issues.title: Qodo AntiSlop scan found 46 issues across 10 recent PRs
source_issues.evidence: Automated scan confirmed bug on main branch (PR #1418). When users specify a model name with a provider prefix (e.g., 'openrouter/llama-3'), the system does not prompt for the required API key, leading to silent failures or cryptic errors.

signals.topic: Blocking time.sleep() in async handler stalls all concurrent requests
signals.summary: A blocking `time.sleep()` call inside an async request handler causes the entire server to stall, blocking all other concurrent requests until the sleep completes.
aliases: server stalls due to sync sleep in async context
signals.review_reason: Confirmed bug (PR #1465) where a sync sleep in an async handler blocks the event loop, stalling all concurrent requests. This is a server reliability issue that degrades multi-user/multi-request scenarios but is not a complete service outage, making it P2 given count=1 and no direct user reports.

source_issues.title: Qodo AntiSlop scan found 46 issues across 10 recent PRs
source_issues.evidence: Automated scan confirmed bug on main branch (PR #1465). A synchronous `time.sleep()` call inside the async request handler blocks the event loop, stalling all other in-flight requests for the duration of the sleep.

signals.topic: LiteLLM model cost map warning flooding logs with unmapped third-party models
signals.summary: When using third-party models (Qwen, DeepSeek, etc.) that are not in LiteLLM's cost map, verbose WARNING logs are emitted repeatedly, degrading observability and user experience.
aliases: unmapped model cost warning for Qwen/DeepSeek
signals.review_reason: Real user-reported issue with confirmed evidence: the user explicitly describes the reproduction steps, environment (Win11, Python 3.11, v0.3.7), and attaches screenshots of the warning. The WARNING floods the logs every time an unmapped third-party model is used. While not a crash, it degrades observability and signals an unhandled edge case in the LiteLLM integration layer. Count=1 and severity is moderate, so P2 is appropriate.

source_issues.title: LiteLLM:WARNING: litellm_logging.py:2323 - Model is not mapped in model cost map
source_issues.evidence: Real user report from 2024-08-17 with 2 comments confirming the issue. User attempted to use Qwen2-72B-Instruct and DeepSeek models via LiteLLM, triggering repeated WARNING logs: 'Model is not mapped in model cost map. Defaulting to None model_cost_information'. Issue filed on v0.3.7, Windows 11, Python 3.11.

signals.topic: Multiple uncaught exceptions crash the application during startup and runtime
signals.summary: Aider crashes with uncaught RuntimeError, OSError, PermissionError, AssertionError, and ModuleNotFoundError across multiple scenarios (symlink loops, file path length limits, permission issues, HTTP client state, config parsing, missing optional deps), completely blocking usage.
signals.review_reason: 8 distinct crash scenarios all uncaught by the application. Each crashes the main workflow (startup, repo scan, /help, /web, /ask) with no user recovery. Combined count 8, each is a high-impact blocking failure. PP-001 merges these under root cause 'uncaught exceptions' — a systemic quality gap, not individual noise.

source_issues.title: Uncaught RuntimeError in pathlib.py line 1237
source_issues.evidence: RuntimeError: Symlink loop crashes aider on startup/repo scan — uncaught, no user recovery path

source_issues.title: Uncaught OSError in pathlib.py line 842
source_issues.evidence: OSError errno 36 'File name too long' crashes aider on startup when --system-message is long — uncaught exception

source_issues.title: Uncaught PermissionError in pathlib.py line 1311
source_issues.evidence: PermissionError: Permission denied on /app/.aider/caches prevents aider from starting — uncaught

source_issues.title: Uncaught AssertionError in configargparse.py line 1128
source_issues.evidence: AssertionError in configargparse crashes aider on startup with certain config values — uncaught

source_issues.title: Uncaught ModuleNotFoundError in scrape.py line 144
source_issues.evidence: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'playwright' crashes /web command — uncaught, blocks web scraping

source_issues.title: Uncaught RuntimeError in _client.py line 901
source_issues.evidence: RuntimeError: Cannot send a request, as the client has been closed crashes /help command on Windows — uncaught

source_issues.title: Uncaught UnicodeEncodeError in utils.py line 139
source_issues.evidence: Uncaught UnicodeEncodeError in utils.py — no body but title confirms crash

source_issues.title: Network unreachable? Not here. Mystery
source_issues.evidence: litellm.InternalServerError misattributed to API provider while actual root cause is network unreachable — user trapped in retry loop with misleading error

signals.topic: Windows console Unicode encoding crash — application crashes on output with cp1252 encoding
signals.summary: On Windows, when the console uses cp1252 encoding (default Windows console), aider crashes with UnicodeEncodeError when outputting characters like \u22ee (vertical ellipsis) that cannot be encoded. Caused by rich library console rendering on Windows.
signals.review_reason: Two identical crash reports on Windows 11 with cp1252 console encoding. The crash occurs during rich library console output (tool_output / repo map rendering), blocking the main user-facing output path. Windows users are left unable to use aider at all when their console codepage doesn't support certain Unicode characters. Consistent, reproducible, blocks core workflow.

source_issues.title: Uncaught UnicodeEncodeError in cp1252.py line 19
source_issues.evidence: UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode character '\u22ee' crashes rich console output on Windows cp1252 — two identical reports from same user, confirmed reproducible on Windows 11 with aider 0.86.2

source_issues.title: Uncaught UnicodeEncodeError in cp1252.py line 19
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of #4986 — same crash on same environment, different timing. Confirms this is a recurring Windows-specific issue.

signals.topic: Argument parsing crashes — overly long values or certain config formats cause uncaught AssertionError, blocking startup
signals.summary: When config files contain non-string values or command-line arguments exceed certain length limits, the configargparse library raises an uncaught AssertionError, preventing aider from starting entirely.
signals.review_reason: Two startup-blocking crashes caused by argument/config parsing edge cases: one from OS-level path length limits being hit during stat() call on a non-path argument, another from config file containing non-string values. Both prevent aider from starting. Root cause is lack of input validation before passing to OS/stat libraries.

source_issues.title: Uncaught OSError in pathlib.py line 842
source_issues.evidence: OSError errno 36 'File name too long' from --system-message value exceeding OS path length limit passed to os.stat() — crashes during argparse path checking before main() runs. Distinct root cause from PP-001 symlink issue.

source_issues.title: Uncaught AssertionError in configargparse.py line 1128
source_issues.evidence: AssertionError: config parser should convert anything that is not a list to string — crashes during parse_known_args on startup with certain config file contents. Blocks user from launching aider.

signals.topic: Network unreachable is misdiagnosed as API provider outage — users trapped in misleading retry loop
signals.summary: When the user's machine cannot reach external endpoints (raw.githubusercontent.com for model metadata), aider repeatedly retries and reports InternalServerError from the API provider, when the real issue is network connectivity. Users waste time waiting and are misled about the root cause.
aliases: Network unreachable misattributed to API provider
litellm misreports network errors as provider errors
signals.review_reason: While only 1 issue, the user impact is significant: the error message actively misleads users into thinking the API provider is down, causing unnecessary waiting and confusion. This is particularly impactful for users in restricted network environments (air-gapped, corporate firewalls). The retry behavior amplifies the problem by wasting time before the user gives up. This is a systemic error-handling gap, not a one-off.

source_issues.title: Network unreachable? Not here. Mystery
source_issues.evidence: User with network-restricted environment (no internet access) runs aider — litellm raises InternalServerError misattributing network unreachable to API provider. Aider retries indefinitely with misleading 'API provider servers are down' messages. Actual root cause is raw.githubusercontent.com being unreachable, not the LLM API. User must Ctrl+C to exit. Clear cost: wasted time, user confusion, inability to use aider in air-gapped or restricted-network environments.

signals.topic: /help command crashes with LLM provider error due to malformed model name in litellm
signals.summary: When a user runs /help with a certain model configuration (claude-haiku-4-6), aider attempts to load an embedding model via litellm with the malformed model name, causing a BadRequestError before help can be displayed. The /help command is a core user-facing feature.
signals.review_reason: Single report but affects a core built-in command (/help). Users lose access to help documentation, which degrades the experience especially for new users. The crash is in the /help command execution path, not an edge case.

source_issues.title: /help token raises error
source_issues.evidence: Running /help how can the edit format be changed triggers litellm.BadRequestError: LLM Provider NOT provided with model=claude-haiku-4-6. The /help command fails to display, blocking users from accessing built-in help documentation.

signals.topic: Node.js version compatibility causing installation and runtime failures
signals.summary: promptfoo 0.121.3 declares a Node.js engine requirement of '^20.20.0 || >=22.22.0' but many users are on v22.21.1, causing npm EBADENGINE warnings and a fatal ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE crash at runtime during redteam eval, completely blocking the main workflow.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow startup crash: users cannot run redteam eval at all on the latest version when using Node v22.21.1, a widely-deployed version. The engine requirement gap (22.21.1 is excluded by >=22.22.0) combined with the ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE runtime error renders the tool unusable for the redteaming use case, which is a core feature.

source_issues.title: Unable to install latest version of promptfoo
source_issues.evidence: npm EBADENGINE warns node v22.21.1 is unsupported, then ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE crashes the process during redteam eval — main workflow completely blocked.

signals.topic: MCP scan fails due to email verification and remote generation requirements blocking pipeline use
signals.summary: Users running MCP scan in CI/CD pipelines (Docker containers) encounter email verification prompts or 'remote generation is disabled' errors, making it impossible to execute scans in automated environments without cloud login.
aliases: MCP scan requires cloud login in CI/CD
Remote generation mandatory for MCP scan
signals.review_reason: This completely blocks the MCP scan feature in automated CI/CD pipelines. Users who have their own API keys (OPENAI_API_KEY set) are told remote generation is disabled, and those without cloud login hit email verification. This is a main-flow failure for a documented feature.

source_issues.title: Unable to run MCP scan - Remote generation mandated
source_issues.evidence: In a Harness pipeline inside Docker, the user cannot run MCP scan without either email verification (cloud login) or enabling remote generation — both incompatible with fully automated CI/CD workflows.

signals.topic: apiKeyRequired config not respected for anthropic:claude-agent-sdk provider
signals.summary: Setting apiKeyRequired: false in the provider config still causes the tool to throw 'Missing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY' error for the anthropic:claude-agent-sdk provider, preventing users with Claude subscriptions (no API key) from using promptfoo.
aliases: Claude subscription users cannot use promptfoo
signals.review_reason: A documented config option (apiKeyRequired) is silently ignored, causing auth failures for a legitimate use case (Claude subscription without API key). This is a clear functional defect that makes a core integration unavailable to affected users.

source_issues.title: apiKeyRequired not working for anthropic:claude-agent-sdk
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly sets apiKeyRequired: false in config but still gets 'Missing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY' error, blocking use for Claude subscription-based authentication.

signals.topic: 'not-javascript' assertion type produces false results for non-boolean value types
signals.summary: The assertion type 'not-javascript' works correctly only when value is a boolean. When value is a function, number, or object, the inverse check is skipped, causing the assertion to incorrectly pass when it should fail (or vice versa).
aliases: not-javascript assertion broken for function/number/object values
signals.review_reason: Assertion evaluation silently produces incorrect pass/fail results for multiple value types. This undermines the reliability of test suites — users cannot trust test outcomes when 'not-javascript' is used with non-boolean values.

source_issues.title: assertion type: "not-javascript" doesn't work in all cases
source_issues.evidence: Assertion with type 'not-javascript' and a function/number/object value incorrectly passes because handleJavascript() only checks the 'inverse' flag for boolean value type, silently giving wrong test results.

signals.topic: crossSessionLeak grader silently bypasses security checks when metadata is missing
signals.summary: When crossSessionLeakMatch metadata is not set, the crossSessionLeak grader passes 'undefined' to String.includes(), coercing it to the string 'undefined'. This causes false positives (LLM output containing 'undefined' fails) and false negatives (security bypass — no leak is ever detected when metadata is missing).
aliases: undefined metadata causes security bypass in red team grader
signals.review_reason: A security testing feature (crossSessionLeak) silently bypasses detection when misconfigured — it never catches real leaks and may flag innocent output. This is a functional defect in a security feature that gives users false confidence in their test results.

source_issues.title: bug: crossSessionLeak grader silently searches for string "undefined" when metadata is missing
source_issues.evidence: Security testing feature silently passes regardless of actual leakage when metadata is missing. The grader coerces undefined to 'undefined' string and searches for it, producing both false positives and false negatives.

signals.topic: ElasticsearchStore sync methods crash in ASGI environments due to run_until_complete event-loop mismatch
signals.summary: ElasticsearchStore wraps all sync methods via asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete(), which fails with 'attached to a different loop' RuntimeError in ASGI deployments (Gunicorn+Uvicorn). This blocks production deployment and prevents connection pooling. Issues #21325 and #21324 are identical reports.
signals.review_reason: Two independent users report a RuntimeError that blocks production ASGI deployments. The crash is confirmed with full stack traces and affects close(), query(), add(), delete() — all core operations. The OpensearchVectorStore in the same codebase already implements the fix pattern, confirming the issue is reproducible and solvable.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: ElasticsearchStore sync methods use run_until_complete — breaks in ASGI with pooled clients
source_issues.evidence: RuntimeError: Task <Task pending> got Future attached to a different loop. Blocks close() in VectorStoreService.__exit__() via sync_to_async. Prevents pooling AsyncElasticsearch clients at process level. The same OpensearchVectorStore already solves this with separate sync/async clients.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: ElasticsearchStore sync methods use run_until_complete — breaks in ASGI with pooled clients
source_issues.evidence: Identical report to #21325. RuntimeError confirmed on llama-index-vector-stores-elasticsearch 0.5.1, Gunicorn+Uvicorn, Python 3.11. Full stack trace showing aiohttp client closing failure.

signals.topic: ElasticsearchStore.query() silently ignores metadata_keyword_suffix on synchronous path
signals.summary: The synchronous query() method accepts metadata_keyword_suffix but never forwards it to aquery(), causing custom metadata suffix filters to silently fall back to the default .keyword suffix with no error or warning.
signals.review_reason: Silent data corruption: metadata filters silently use the wrong suffix with no error or warning. Users relying on custom metadata suffix fields for access control or filtering get incorrect query results. The async path works correctly, making this a regression for sync-only users.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: ElasticsearchStore.query() ignores metadata_keyword_suffix on the synchronous path
source_issues.evidence: Sync wrapper accepts metadata_keyword_suffix parameter but call forwards only (query, custom_query, es_filter, **kwargs) — custom suffix never reaches async impl. No exception thrown; filter silently uses wrong suffix. Observed on main at commit 59ca0b65b.

signals.topic: IngestionPipeline with num_workers > 1 silently discards all cache writes
signals.summary: When IngestionPipeline runs with multiple workers, cache entries written inside worker processes are lost because the worker-side cache copies are not merged back into the parent process. This causes expensive transformations like embedding to be re-executed on every multi-worker run, with no cache benefit.
aliases: pipeline.persist() misses worker process cache entries
signals.review_reason: Deterministic reproduction with provided code snippet. Silent performance regression: multi-worker pipelines are explicitly used for speed but lose all caching, causing re-execution of expensive embedding steps on every run. This defeats the purpose of multi-worker ingestion and causes direct cost impact in production.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: IngestionPipeline with `num_workers > 1` silently loses all cache writes
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible with provided code: multi-worker first run cache size=0, second run cache size=0. Sequential run works correctly (cache size=1). Root cause: self.cache is passed to workers, each mutates its own copy which is lost on exit. pipeline.persist() also excludes worker-created entries, meaning cache is not recoverable.

signals.topic: ChromaDB MAX_CHUNK_SIZE hardcoded value causes batch insert failure on some SQLite configurations
signals.summary: ChromaVectorStore hardcodes MAX_CHUNK_SIZE=41665, but ChromaDB's actual dynamic max batch size varies by SQLite platform. Inserting many documents fails with chromadb.errors.InternalError: Batch size exceeds max batch size, even when resources are not constrained.
aliases: ChromaVectorStore hardcoded batch size causes InternalError
signals.review_reason: Confirmed InternalError on insert operation due to hardcoded constant. The fix is straightforward (use get_max_batch_size() API), and the issue blocks any user on platforms where the hardcoded threshold exceeds the platform limit.

source_issues.title: ChromaDB MAX_CHUNK_SIZE does not take into account platform-dependent limits
source_issues.evidence: chromadb.errors.InternalError: ValueError: Batch size of 6401 is greater than max batch size of 5461. Root cause confirmed: hardcoded 41665 in llama_index code, but chromadb 1.2.0 exposes get_max_batch_size() API. Verified on Python 3.13.7, sqlite 3.50.4, chromadb 1.2.0.

signals.topic: VectorStoreIndex semantic bleed at section boundaries degrades retrieval precision in dense financial documents
signals.summary: Adjacent sections in financial filings (10-K) share terminology but are semantically distinct. Top-k retrieval surfaces chunks from neighboring sections, causing LLM to answer from wrong section. Affects production RAG on SEC filings.
aliases: semantic bleed section boundaries retrieval precision
signals.review_reason: Retrieval precision regression in production RAG for financial documents. While no crash occurs, the LLM consistently answers from wrong document sections, which in financial use cases can mean compliance violations or incorrect advice. The triage label and bug designation indicate the team acknowledges this as a defect.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Semantic bleed at section boundaries in VectorStoreIndex on 10‑K filings degrades retrieval precision
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible on 0.11.0 with standard 512-1024 token chunking. Specific test cases: Risk Factors vs Legal Proceedings and MD&A sections return each other's chunks as top results. No crash, but LLM answers from wrong section, directly degrading QA accuracy in a financial compliance context.

signals.topic: MCP server memory database fails to initialize — blocks primary deployment mode
signals.summary: Memory database initialization does not propagate to MCP server process, causing all memory operations to fail. Combined with global install cwd misconfiguration, this breaks ALL file operations for macOS users.
signals.review_reason: Two confirmed issues (#1524, #1532) with distinct root causes both breaking MCP primary deployment mode. #1524: MCP process starts with uninitialized DB, making memory features non-functional. #1532: macOS global install defaults cwd to '/', making all file operations fail for every affected user. Together these block the advertised MCP integration use case entirely.

source_issues.title: MCP Server: Memory database not initializing - memory_store fails with 'Database not initialized'
source_issues.evidence: MCP server starts with fresh uninitialized in-memory DB. CLI init doesn't persist to MCP process. memory_store fails. memory_list returns empty. embeddings_init fails silently. Blocks primary deployment mode (Claude Desktop MCP integration) — the core use case for persistent context optimization.

source_issues.title: Bug: Global install registers MCP server without cwd, causing all file ops to fail on macOS (process.cwd() = '/')
source_issues.evidence: Global install via quickstart spawns MCP stdio process with no cwd on macOS. Defaults to '/'. All process.cwd()-based path resolution targets /.claude-flow/ (read-only). ALL file operations fail silently or throw ENOENT/EACCES for every macOS global-install user. Affects memory_store, swarm_init, agent_spawn, session_save, github_repo_analyze and ~20 tools.

signals.topic: Intelligence hooks cause indefinite CLI hangs / ~20s latency on every interaction
signals.summary: Intelligence layer runs synchronous PageRank on 150MB+ JSON files on every session start and end, causing CLI to hang indefinitely or add 18-21s latency per prompt.
signals.review_reason: Two reports of CLI completely unusable with ruflo hooks installed. #1531: intelligence.init/consolidate never completed in testing (killed at 18-35s). #1530: 18-21s latency per prompt. Both are session-start and session-end blocking — the most fundamental interaction points. Not edge cases: these fire on every single Claude Code run.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Intelligence hooks cause indefinite hang — PageRank on 150MB JSON blocks every CLI interaction
source_issues.evidence: intelligence.init() reads 150MB JSON (94MB graph-state.json + 32MB ranked-context.json + 23MB auto-memory-store.json), builds 18,014-node graph, runs synchronous PageRank — never completed in testing (killed at 18-35s). session-end hook consistently fails (10s timeout exceeded by 35s+ function). Every interaction requires Ctrl+C. 94GB RAM, 24-core system — not resource-constrained.

source_issues.title: Hooks causing ~20s latency on every Claude Code CLI interaction
source_issues.evidence: .claude/settings.json registers 11+ hooks across 9 lifecycle events, each spawning Node.js subprocess. ~18-21s per prompt vs 4.8s baseline. session-end hook consistently fails. Same user/system as #1531, same underlying hook system.

signals.topic: Intelligence auto-memory silently drops all session data on every session
signals.summary: Auto-memory hook silently discards all session memory data due to cross-package import failure. Data writes succeed but are lost on process exit. Also causes 194MB graph-state.json bloat.
signals.review_reason: Two confirmed data-integrity bugs in intelligence.cjs. #1526: every session's hook-written memory is silently discarded (data loss, no error). #1518: same deduplication bug causes 194MB disk bloat and constant O(n^2) reprocessing. Both are systematic data integrity failures that degrade or destroy the self-learning memory layer advertised as a core feature.

source_issues.title: fix: auto-memory hook silently drops all session data + 4 packaging bugs
source_issues.evidence: AgentDBBackend does cross-package import('@claude-flow/agentdb') which fails silently. Falls back to in-memory Map. All hook-written memory is discarded on process exit — no error, no warning. ID collision separately causes 4,482 entries to collapse to 157 unique, compounding data loss. better-sqlite3 as optional dep allows 0 controllers state.

source_issues.title: Bug: intelligence.cjs graph-state.json grows to 194MB due to duplicate store entries
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate entries (4,482 total, 157 unique) cause O(n^2) edge generation (1.3M edges → 194MB graph-state.json). Cache-hit check never matches (compares deduplicated count vs raw count), forcing full graph rebuild every session. 194MB file on disk. Related root cause to #1526 (same deduplication bug in intelligence.cjs).

signals.topic: ruvector CLI hardcodes pgvector extension instead of detecting ruvector
signals.summary: ruvector init/status/benchmark/optimize hardcode 'pgvector' extension check but the official ruvector-postgres Docker image ships the ruvector extension. Init and migrate commands fail, blocking setup.
aliases: ruvector benchmark type vector does not exist
signals.review_reason: Two confirmed issues (#1522, #1520) showing ruvector CLI tooling is broken against the official ruvector-postgres Docker image. Init, migrate, status, and benchmark all fail. However: this only affects users of the ruvector PostgreSQL backend (a specific optional feature), not the general user base. Downgraded to P2 based on narrower scope.

source_issues.title: ruvector init fails: checks for pgvector instead of ruvector extension, blocks migrate
source_issues.evidence: init hardcodes 'CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector' (pgvector). Official ruvector-postgres Docker image ships ruvector extension v0.3.0. init fails with 'pgvector not installed'. migrate fails with 'relation claude_flow.migrations does not exist'. Blocks entire ruvector PostgreSQL setup.

source_issues.title: ruvector CLI subcommands hardcode pgvector instead of detecting ruvector extension
source_issues.evidence: status reports false negative 'pgvector not installed' when ruvector 0.3.0 is installed. benchmark fails with 'ERROR: type vector does not exist'. Both status and benchmark commands are broken for every ruvector-postgres user.

signals.topic: Memory subcommands hang indefinitely after successful completion
signals.summary: ruflo memory store and memory search complete their operation in ~3-5ms but the Node process never exits. Requires manual Ctrl+C or background+sleep+kill workaround.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed regression: operation completes correctly (3ms, correct output) but process hangs indefinitely. Every programmatic use of ruflo memory tools requires the background+sleep+kill workaround — a blocking UX failure for scripting. MCP path also affected since it shares the same memory infrastructure. Regression indicates the underlying event-loop leak is not fully resolved.

source_issues.title: Memory subcommands still hang on v3.5.75 — original fix in #1453 appears incomplete
source_issues.evidence: ruflo memory store and memory search complete successfully in 3-5ms with correct output, but process never exits. Workaround requires background+sleep+kill pattern. Blocks all programmatic/script use. MCP path also affected (same underlying event loop issue). Regression from #1453 which was supposedly fixed on 2026-04-02 but symptom persists in v3.5.75.

signals.topic: Navigation leaves browser at about:blank after form submission or SPA navigation — blocks authentication workflows
signals.summary: CDP target switches to about:blank after form submission or SPA navigation, even though the actual page has navigated. All subsequent commands operate on a dead page, making agent-browser unusable for any workflow requiring authentication via form submission. Regression from v0.24.x.
signals.review_reason: Three separate issues (1157, 1177, 1138) all report the same root symptom: browser ends up at about:blank after navigation. Issue 1157 explicitly blocks authentication workflows (form submission login), and issue 1177 is a confirmed regression in v0.24.1 affecting headless CI — a primary use case. This is a main-flow failure that prevents agents from completing authenticated sessions.

source_issues.title: CDP target lost after form submission / SPA navigation — tab becomes about:blank
source_issues.evidence: After submitting a login form (email/password → Enter or button click), the active CDP target switches to about:blank and all subsequent commands operate on a dead page. Makes agent-browser unusable for any workflow that requires authentication via form submission.

source_issues.title: open command navigates to about:blank since 0.24.1 (headless CI)
source_issues.evidence: Since upgrading from 0.24.0 to 0.24.1, the open command leaves the browser on about:blank instead of navigating to the target URL. Persists in 0.25.0 and 0.25.1. Affects headless CI on Ubuntu GitHub Actions runner.

source_issues.title: AgentCore: open returns EOF / about:blank and leaves orphaned READY sessions
source_issues.evidence: agent-browser 0.24.0 with -p agentcore: open often fails with 'Invalid response: EOF while parsing a value'. Browser remains at about:blank. Multiple orphaned READY AgentCore sessions left behind.

signals.topic: Chrome process killed after ~7 seconds in v0.24.1 — PR_SET_PDEATHSIG threading regression with tokio multi-threaded runtime
signals.summary: v0.24.1 introduced prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, SIGKILL) in Chrome's pre_exec hook. Tokios multi-threaded runtime recycles worker threads after idle periods, causing the kernel to send SIGKILL to Chrome whenever the spawning thread exits. Agents lose their browser session mid-operation after ~7 seconds of inactivity.
aliases: Chrome killed by PR_SET_PDEATHSIG tokio regression
signals.review_reason: Regression in v0.24.1 confirmed via root cause analysis. Chrome silently dying after idle periods breaks all long-running agent workflows, which is the primary use case. While count=1, the severity (complete session loss mid-operation) and clear regression evidence justify P1 over P2.

source_issues.title: fix: PR_SET_PDEATHSIG kills Chrome in tokio multi-threaded runtime (v0.24.1 regression)
source_issues.evidence: PR_SET_PDEATHSIG tracks the thread that called fork(), not the process. Tokio multi-threaded runtime recycles the worker thread that spawned Chrome after a few seconds of idle time — when the thread exits, kernel sends SIGKILL to Chrome. This is a v0.24.1 regression that kills all browser sessions after ~7 seconds of idle.

signals.topic: AGENT_BROWSER_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT environment variable not honoured — operations hang indefinitely
signals.summary: Setting AGENT_BROWSER_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT does not affect CLI operations. The timeout is not applied when waiting for selectors or other blocking operations, causing agents to hang indefinitely instead of failing gracefully after the configured duration.
signals.review_reason: Env var is completely ignored, causing infinite hangs — a clear operational failure for agents relying on timeouts for resilience. While count=1, the impact (indefinite hang blocking agent pipelines) and explicit user evidence meet the P1 bar despite the fix being in progress.

source_issues.title: AGENT_BROWSER_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT not honoured in the cli
source_issues.evidence: Setting AGENT_BROWSER_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT env variable while waiting for selector does not honour the timeout — it keeps waiting infinitely instead of failing after the specified timeout. Issue closed with fix.

signals.topic: CLI unusable in Claude Code sandbox due to Unix domain socket syscall restrictions
signals.summary: All agent-browser CLI commands fail in Claude Code sandbox because the daemon relies on Unix domain socket IPC, which is blocked by the sandbox's syscall restrictions (bind/connect syscalls). This renders the tool completely non-functional in a specific but legitimate environment.
aliases: Unix socket daemon blocked by Claude Code sandbox
agent-browser CLI fails in sandbox environment
signals.review_reason: Complete CLI unavailability in a specific environment (Claude Code sandbox) is a functional blocker. While count=1, the nature of the failure (total tool unusability in a legitimate use case) with a clear proposed workaround justifies P1.

source_issues.title: CLI unusable in Claude Code sandbox: Unix domain socket bind/connect blocked
source_issues.evidence: All agent-browser CLI commands fail inside the Claude Code sandbox because the daemon requires Unix domain socket IPC, which is blocked by the sandbox's syscall restrictions. User explicitly requests a --no-daemon or --direct mode using TCP/CDP WebSocket.

signals.topic: State persistence (cookies / localStorage) broken on Linux — session save/restore fails to restore browser state
signals.summary: On Linux, --session-name auto-save/restore and state save/--state both fail to restore cookies and localStorage across restarts. The JSON files contain the correct data but the browser relaunches without them restored, breaking session continuity.
signals.review_reason: State persistence is explicitly broken — saved cookies and localStorage are not restored on relaunch on Linux, breaking session continuity for any agent workflow that needs to resume authenticated sessions. Clearly documented with evidence of the gap.

source_issues.title: Linux v0.24.1: state save/--state and --session-name write state but do not restore cookies or localStorage
source_issues.evidence: On Linux with agent-browser 0.24.1, both --session-name auto-save/restore and state save followed by --state on relaunch fail to restore state. Saved JSON contains expected cookie and localStorage entry, but next launch comes back with neither restored.

signals.topic: react-best-practices skill provides incorrect Next.js SSR patterns causing runtime errors when users follow the guidance
signals.summary: The `bundle-defer-third-party` and `bundle-dynamic-imports` rules in the react-best-practices skill show `ssr: false` with `next/dynamic` used inside Server Components, which Next.js explicitly prohibits — throwing a runtime error. Users following the skill guidance would encounter this error in production, making the skill guidance actively misleading and functionally broken.
signals.review_reason: This is a workflow-runtime issue where the skill's documented code patterns are incorrect. Users following the skill guidance would encounter a hard runtime error in Next.js, making the skill actively harmful and misleading. The issue is well-documented with Next.js official docs references and specific file locations. Count=1 limits it to P1, not P0.

source_issues.title: react-best-practices: ssr: false used without 'use client' in bundle-defer-third-party and bundle-dynamic-imports
source_issues.evidence: The skill rules provide code examples using `ssr: false` with `next/dynamic` in a Server Component context, which Next.js explicitly throws an error for at runtime: 'ssr: false is not allowed with next/dynamic in Server Components. Please move it into a Client Component.' Users copying the example would get a broken build.

signals.topic: SKILL.md upload fails with 'XML tags not allowed' error blocking skill publishing workflow
signals.summary: When attempting to upload a `.zip` file (specifically react-view-transitions.zip) to the Claude skills section, the upload fails with the error 'SKILL.md description cannot contain XML tags'. This blocks users from publishing their skills, representing a functional failure of the core upload workflow.
aliases: skill zip upload XML tag error
skill publishing blocked by XML validation
signals.review_reason: This is a direct workflow-blocking issue. The upload mechanism rejects valid skill zips with an opaque XML tag validation error, preventing the core publishing action. While count=1, the evidence is unambiguous — a user tried to publish and was blocked. This is a functional failure of the primary use case (publishing skills), warranting P1.

source_issues.title: Upload Fails with "SKILL.md description cannot contain XML tags" Error
source_issues.evidence: User attempted to upload react-view-transitions.zip and received the blocking error 'SKILL.md description cannot contain XML tags'. The upload workflow fails and the user is prevented from publishing the skill.

signals.topic: AI Gateway provider failover breaks with provider-incompatible conversation history (Google thought signatures rejected by Vertex)
signals.summary: When AI Gateway fails over mid-conversation from Google to Vertex, Vertex rejects the request with 400 because Google's thought signatures are incompatible, completely defeating the fallback mechanism and leaving users with no recovery path during transient provider outages.
aliases: AI Gateway Google to Vertex failover failure
mid-conversation provider failover rejected by backup provider
signals.review_reason: Gateway failover is a core resilience feature. When it fails, users have no automatic recovery from transient provider outages — they must manually configure workarounds that sacrifice the fallback entirely. The issue is reproducible with clear steps and affects the intended multi-provider resilience pattern.

source_issues.title: AI Gateway: Vertex rejects thought signatures from Google AI Studio on mid-conversation failover
source_issues.evidence: Multi-step agent session (10+ tool calls) runs fine on Google, but on step 11 when Google returns 503, Gateway fails over to Vertex which immediately rejects with 400 'Thought signature is not valid'. Full conversation history including Google-generated thought signatures is sent to Vertex. Workaround requires disabling failover entirely, losing Vertex as fallback.

signals.topic: AI SDK drops empty text blocks causing Bedrock validation errors and message index corruption in multi-turn reasoning conversations
signals.summary: The AI SDK strips empty text blocks from assistant responses when using Bedrock with reasoning/thinking content. This corrupts the message content block indices sent back to Bedrock in subsequent requests, triggering a rejection error: 'The model cannot modify thinking or redacted_thinking blocks in assistant messages'. Every multi-turn conversation using Bedrock reasoning blocks eventually fails.
aliases: empty text block stripping corrupts message indices
Bedrock thinking block validation error after SDK processing
signals.review_reason: This blocks every multi-turn Bedrock conversation that uses reasoning/thinking content — a core use case. The message index corruption is silent in the first turn but causes guaranteed failure in subsequent turns, making long-running agents unusable on Bedrock.

source_issues.title: AI SDK drops "" reasoning blocks but these MUST be included for validation
source_issues.evidence: Bedrock response has 5 content blocks including empty text. After SDK strips empty text, only 4 blocks are sent in next request, causing indices to shift. Bedrock rejects the modified reasoning/thinking blocks with: 'The model cannot modify thinking or redacted_thinking blocks in assistant messages'. Occurs in every multi-turn Bedrock session with reasoning. Confirmed with reproduction steps and code-level trace of the issue.

signals.topic: AI Gateway BYOK Bedrock routing fails silently with empty region in endpoint URL, silently falling back and defeating BYOK purpose
signals.summary: When using AI Gateway with BYOK AWS credentials for Bedrock, every request to Anthropic models fails at the Bedrock attempt due to an empty region segment in the endpoint URL (bedrock-runtime..amazonaws.com). The failure is completely silent at the application level, adding per-request latency from the failed attempt, and BYOK Bedrock credentials are never actually used — all traffic falls back to Anthropic direct API.
aliases: AI Gateway BYOK Bedrock empty region DNS failure
Bedrock BYOK credentials unusable due to malformed endpoint URL
signals.review_reason: The failure is silent (no application-level error) yet occurs on every single request that should use BYOK Bedrock, adding latency and making a core enterprise feature entirely non-functional. Users cannot detect the problem without inspecting providerMetadata.routing.

source_issues.title: AI Gateway BYOK Bedrock routing fails with empty region in endpoint URL
source_issues.evidence: Every Anthropic model request fails at Bedrock attempt with ENOTFOUND for bedrock-runtime..amazonaws.com. Routing metadata shows finalProvider: anthropic (not bedrock). BYOK credentials are never used — request silently falls back to Anthropic direct with system credentials. No error thrown at application level. Users cannot leverage BYOK Bedrock pricing/quotas at all.

signals.topic: Anthropic web search tool (webSearch_20260209) crashes toUIMessageStreamResponse with TypeError
signals.summary: Using Anthropic's native web search tool with streamText and toUIMessageStreamResponse causes a server-side TypeError crash: 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading type)'. The server returns HTTP 200 but the client receives no usable response. This completely blocks the UI streaming path when Anthropic web search is enabled.
aliases: Anthropic native web search TypeError crash
toUIMessageStreamResponse undefined type crash with web search
server crash on Anthropic web search tool use
signals.review_reason: This is a server-side crash that makes a first-party Anthropic feature entirely unusable with the SDK's UI streaming path. The crash is deterministic and reproducible, blocking the user-facing stream response when web search is enabled.

source_issues.title: Anthropic web search tool (webSearch_20260209) crashes toUIMessageStreamResponse with TypeError
source_issues.evidence: Server throws TypeError during stream serialization when Anthropic returns server_tool_use and web_search_tool_result content blocks. POST returns 200 but client receives no usable response. Crash is deterministic when web search tool is used. Workaround requires replacing Anthropic's native tool with a custom DuckDuckGo scraping implementation.

signals.topic: Amazon Bedrock explicit access keys incorrectly merge AWS_SESSION_TOKEN from environment, causing auth failures on EKS/ECS/Lambda
signals.summary: When passing explicit accessKeyId and secretAccessKey to createAmazonBedrock, the SDK still attaches AWS_SESSION_TOKEN from the environment. On EKS IRSA, ECS task roles, and Lambda (which always set this variable), the merged credentials are invalid and AWS returns 'The security token included in the request is invalid'. The workaround requires wrapping keys in a credentialProvider function, which is non-obvious and undocumented.
aliases: Amazon Bedrock AWS_SESSION_TOKEN merge with explicit credentials
EKS IRSA auth failure with explicit Bedrock credentials
Bedrock credential resolution ignores explicit key override
signals.review_reason: A common deployment pattern (explicit credentials on cloud hosts) is broken by implicit credential merging. The auth failure is silent in some environments (works locally where AWS_SESSION_TOKEN is unset) but fails in production on EKS/ECS/Lambda, making this a deployment-time surprise with no clear error message.

source_issues.title: @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock: explicit accessKeyId/secretAccessKey should not merge AWS_SESSION_TOKEN from env
source_issues.evidence: Explicitly providing accessKeyId + secretAccessKey still causes AWS 'The security token included in the request is invalid' error on hosts that set AWS_SESSION_TOKEN (EKS IRSA, ECS, Lambda). Downstream report confirms issue in production: https://github.com/8monkey-ai/hebo-platform/issues/351. 2 comments indicate active discussion and confirmation.

signals.topic: Vulnerable lodash@4.17.23 (CVE-2026-4800) bundled in Next.js dist/compiled — cannot be remediated via npm audit
signals.summary: Next.js ships lodash@4.17.23 in its vendored pre-compiled `dist/compiled/` files (jsonwebtoken/index.js, babel-packages/packages-bundle.js). This version is affected by CVE-2026-4800 (code injection via _.template). Downstream users cannot fix this via `npm audit fix` or `dependencyOverrides` because the code is pre-compiled. Multiple users confirmed.
signals.review_reason: Multiple users independently reported the same CVE in the bundled distribution. This blocks users from passing security audits and is not fixable via standard npm tooling since lodash is pre-compiled inside Next.js distribution files. Clear production impact.

source_issues.title: Vulnerable lodash@4.17.23 bundled in dist/compiled (CVE-2026-4800)
source_issues.evidence: Identical report to #92453. User demonstrates lodash@4.17.23 in jsonwebtoken/index.js and babel-packages/packages-bundle.js. OWASP Dependency-Check flags GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc. Cannot be fixed via npm audit fix or dependency overrides.

source_issues.title: Vulnerable lodash@4.17.23 bundled in dist/compiled (CVE-2026-4800)
source_issues.evidence: User demonstrates Next.js 16.2.2 ships lodash@4.17.23 in vendored dist/compiled/ files. Affected by CVE-2026-4800 (code injection via _.template). Downstream consumers cannot resolve via npm audit fix or dependency overrides since code is pre-compiled.

signals.topic: Turbopack dev: infinite Suspense remount cycle with React.lazy() + 15+ useSyncExternalStore selectors
signals.summary: Turbopack dev mode causes infinite unmount/remount cycles for React.lazy() components with 15+ useSyncExternalStore selectors. Components with fewer selectors work fine. The page never becomes interactive. Webpack dev mode and production builds are unaffected. Reported by two independent users.
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports confirm the same Turbopack-specific bug. Pages with complex state management (15+ store selectors) are completely broken in Turbopack dev mode — the default in Next.js 16. The only workaround requires conditional eager imports that complicate production code.

source_issues.title: [Turbopack] Infinite Suspense remount cycle with React.lazy() + 15+ useSyncExternalStore selectors
source_issues.evidence: Open issue. User provides reproduction repo and detailed analysis. Mount ID tracking confirms unmount/remount (not re-render). Stub component works; full component with 15+ store selectors triggers infinite loop. Threshold around 10-15 selectors. next dev --webpack works perfectly.

source_issues.title: [Turbopack] Infinite Suspense remount cycle with React.lazy() + complex hook trees (15+ useSyncExternalStore)
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate report of same issue by different user (mmmprod vs different author). Same root cause: 15+ useSyncExternalStore selectors with React.lazy + Turbopack dev. Workaround provided (eager import in dev). Very detailed diagnostic evidence with mount ID tracking.

signals.topic: export type in "use server" file causes runtime ReferenceError (regression in v16.1.0+)
signals.summary: Using `export type` in files with the `"use server"` directive causes a runtime ReferenceError in Next.js v16.1.x. PR #86296 refactored server action registration to unconditionally register all exports in a post-pass, without checking `is_type_only`, so TypeScript-erased type exports still get registered as Server Action references — leading to `ReferenceError` at runtime. This is a regression from v16.0.3 where it worked correctly.
signals.review_reason: Regression in a core feature (Server Actions) that breaks user code at runtime with a clear root cause. Affects any user who re-exports types from a server action file — a legitimate and common pattern. Workaround requires modifying source code, making it a real pain point.

source_issues.title: export type in "use server" file causes runtime ReferenceError in v16.1.x (regression from PR #86296)
source_issues.evidence: Runtime ReferenceError: Foo is not defined when using `export type { Foo }` in a `"use server"` file. Root cause explicitly identified in PR #86296 post-pass registration that ignores `is_type_only`. Verified on v16.1.5, works on v16.0.3. Workaround exists but changes user code.

signals.topic: beforeFiles rewrites with locale:false and has conditions broken in v16.2.0+ (Pages Router)
signals.summary: Pages Router beforeFiles rewrites with `locale: false` and `has` query conditions stopped working in v16.2.0. This breaks third-party integrations (e.g. Makeswift visual editor) that depend on these rewrites to intercept preview token requests. Verified as regression through version bisect (last working: v16.1.7).
aliases: beforeFiles locale false has condition broken
signals.review_reason: Regression that breaks a third-party commercial product (Makeswift) by silently breaking rewrite rules. The rewrite config is present in build output but not firing, making diagnosis non-obvious. Version bisect confirms it was working in v16.1.7.

source_issues.title: beforeFiles rewrites with locale: false and has conditions stopped firing in 16.2.0
source_issues.evidence: Makeswift visual editor integration broken in v16.2.0+ — relies on beforeFiles rewrite with locale:false and has query condition. Version bisect confirms: v16.1.7 works, v16.2.0+ broken. Affects a commercial product used by real customers.

signals.topic: Memory leak in standalone output causes OOM crashes in production (fix not backported to stable)
signals.summary: A memory leak in standalone output mode causes continuous memory growth leading to OOM crashes in Docker/ECS production environments on Next.js stable v16.2.2. PR #88577 was merged into canary on 2026-02-10 fixing this, but it was never backported to stable. Users are experiencing production OOM crashes.
signals.review_reason: Production OOM crashes are a severe, blocking issue. The fix was merged and verified in canary but never backported to stable, leaving production users vulnerable. The root cause (clone-response.ts memory leak) is confirmed and fix exists — the pain is the lack of backport, not the unknown root cause.

source_issues.title: PR #88577 fixes memory leak in canary but has not been backported to stable (16.2.2)
source_issues.evidence: User reports OOM crashes in Docker/ECS production on v16.2.2 stable with standalone output. clone-response.ts tee's every response internally causing ArrayBuffer retention. PR #88577 merged into canary Feb 2026 fixing the issue. Cannot test canary in their production Docker environment. Issues #90433 and #90898 also closed without backporting.

signals.topic: Dirty .gitignore causes node_modules to leak into task input hashes, permanently breaking turbo cache
signals.summary: Since v2.8.18, any uncommitted modification to .gitignore causes turbo to stop respecting its patterns during task input hashing. node_modules/ files leak into task inputs, producing different hashes on every run and permanently breaking local/remote cache until the .gitignore change is committed. This is a normal workflow (editing .gitignore before committing) that silently disables all caching.
aliases: gitignored files leak into input hash
signals.review_reason: This is a P1 because it directly breaks the core caching mechanism in a version regression. The issue is reproducible with a minimal script, and the user impact is significant: cache is permanently disabled during a normal workflow (editing .gitignore). The count is 1 because only one issue explicitly documents this regression, but the severity is elevated by the fact it's a regression from v2.8.17 to v2.8.18.

source_issues.title: Dirty .gitignore causes gitignored files to leak into task input hashes (v2.8.18+)
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with minimal repro script. When .gitignore is dirty, node_modules/.bin/foo leaks into inputs (5 inputs vs expected 4). Regression introduced in v2.8.18, likely by PR #12339. Cache permanently broken until .gitignore is committed. In large monorepos turbo walks hundreds of thousands of files in node_modules/ on every invocation.

signals.topic: Turbo crashes (spawnSync UNKNOWN) on Windows when installed via Bun package manager
signals.summary: On Windows, running `bun run build` in a fresh turbo repo crashes with `spawnSync` errors trying to execute the windows-64 turbo binary. Windows security may also block the turbo.exe binary entirely. The build flow is completely blocked.
aliases: turbo.exe blocked by Windows security bun
signals.review_reason: This is a P0 because it completely blocks the main build flow (turbo run build) for users on Windows using Bun as the package manager. The crash is reproducible, the error is an unhandled exception (not graceful degradation), and the Windows security blocking of turbo.exe indicates a code signing/trust issue that affects all Windows users with similar configurations.

source_issues.title: Bun run build failed on window on fresh turbo repo
source_issues.evidence: User on Windows 10/11 with Node.js v25.4.0 reports complete build failure. Error: spawnSync with UNKNOWN errno on turbo.exe. Windows Security popup appeared: 'Part of this app has been blocked — Some features of Node.js JavaScript Runtime may not work because we can't confirm who published turbo.exe that the app tried to load.' Both local and global bun-installed turbo fail identically.

signals.topic: turbo prune --docker corrupts bun.lock with phantom npm packages, breaking bun install --frozen-lockfile in Docker builds
signals.summary: v2.8.16 introduced a regression where `turbo prune --docker` injects ~700 phantom npm package entries (like @gar/promise-retry, @npmcli/*, @sigstore/*, cacache, libnpm*) into bun.lock that don't exist in the original lockfile. This causes `bun install --frozen-lockfile` to fail, completely breaking Docker container builds that depend on prune output.
signals.review_reason: This is a P0 because it blocks a critical CI/CD workflow: Docker container builds using `turbo prune --docker`. The regression in v2.8.16 corrupts the lockfile in a way that fails `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, forcing users to downgrade to 2.8.15. This is a main流程阻断 for teams using bun + Docker + turborepo in production.

source_issues.title: turbo prune --docker injects phantom npm packages into bun.lock (v2.8.16 regression from #12228)
source_issues.evidence: Regression from PR #12228. Diff shows ~700 phantom entries added to bun.lock. bun install --frozen-lockfile correctly rejects structural mismatch. User must pin turbo to 2.8.15 as workaround. Affects any bun monorepo with multiple workspaces using prune --docker for CI/CD container builds.

signals.topic: Tasks randomly skipped due to daemon package discovery timing out and using stale local strategy fallback
signals.summary: When turbo runs in daemon mode, the primary package discovery strategy sometimes times out and falls back to a local strategy. This causes only a subset of tasks to be discovered and run (e.g., 1 instead of 15), silently skipping critical tasks like tsc, lint, and test without any error message. The behavior is non-deterministic — running the same command multiple times produces different results.
signals.review_reason: This is a P0 because it silently skips critical tasks (tsc, lint, test) in a non-deterministic way. Users cannot trust turbo's output — the same command produces different results on consecutive runs. The evidence shows the root cause in debug logs (daemon timeout → fallback → incomplete discovery). With 52 comments, this is a well-known issue. The impact is severe: type errors, lint errors, and test failures go undetected because tasks are silently skipped.

source_issues.title: Tasks getting skipped with no explanation
source_issues.evidence: User runs turbo tsc expecting 15 tasks. Sometimes gets all 15 (correct), sometimes gets only 1 (wrong). Debug logs show daemon's primary strategy timing out and falling back to local strategy: 'primary strategy timed out, attempting fallback strategy'. The fallback fails to discover all packages. 52 comments indicate this is a known recurring issue. TypeScript compilation silently skipped means type errors go undetected.

signals.topic: turbo prune produces different file hashes for files with CRLF line endings, causing remote cache misses
signals.summary: Running `turbo prune` changes the hashes of files that use CRLF line endings compared to their original state. This causes remote cache misses since the hash before and after pruning differs for identical files. The issue may be related to .gitattributes handling of line endings.
aliases: prune CRLF line endings hash mismatch
file hash changes after prune CRLF
signals.review_reason: This is a P1 because it breaks remote cache correctness for any project using CRLF line endings (common on Windows). Hash mismatches after prune mean remote cache artifacts are unreliable. While count=1, the impact extends to any cross-platform monorepo using remote caching with prune, making it a systemic issue beyond a single user.

source_issues.title: Pruning results in different hashes for files with CRLF line endings
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction repo provided at github.com/cjquines/turborepo-gitattributes/. File hashes for files with CRLF line endings differ before and after running turbo prune. This affects remote cache correctness — artifacts cached after prune won't match the original files. Likely related to .gitattributes handling.

signals.topic: CLI `vc link` 链接到错误项目导致部署到错误目标
signals.summary: 用户执行 `vc link` 时，即使传入正确的项目名称或 projectId，CLI 仍会链接到名称相似的另一个项目，并将错误的 OIDC Token 写入配置，导致后续 `vc deploy` 部署到错误的项目。
aliases: CLI project linking picks wrong project
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：用户无法将本地代码链接到正确项目并部署，核心工作流被破坏。即使指定了正确的 projectId 也无法避免，属于明确的项目混淆问题，用户需要手动修复配置才能继续工作。

source_issues.title: CLI: I can't deploy because `vc link` keeps linking wrong project
source_issues.evidence: 用户有两个名称相似的项目 covillage-portal 和 covillage，使用 vc link 指定 projectId 链接 covillage-portal，CLI 显示链接成功但下载的却是 covillage 的环境变量，并将错误的 OIDC Token 写入配置，导致后续所有部署都进入错误的 covillage 项目。

signals.topic: CLI `vercel env add` 在 preview 环境变量添加时强制交互提示，无法在 CI/CD 中使用

aliases: vercel env add interactive prompt CI/CD failure
env add preview git branch prompt blocking automation
signals.review_reason: 关键自动化流程阻断：用户在 CI/CD 环境中完全无法通过 CLI 添加 preview 环境变量，主流程被强制阻断。用户被迫转向直接调用 Vercel REST API 作为 workaround，说明这是真实且持续的使用场景中的阻塞问题。

source_issues.title: CLI: `vercel env add <name> preview` always prompts for git branch even with --yes --force
